literature.headline_zh: SARS-CoV-2本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期SARS-CoV-2研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 在巴基斯坦,XBB.1 及其子变体在 2023 年占主导地位,JN.1 及其子变体持续到 2024 年。虽然到 2024 年中期出现了 KP.2、LB.1 和 LA.1 变体,但 JN.1 仍然占主导地位。相比之下,美国、英国和法国的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 显示,到 2024 年 9 月,XBB.1.5 转变为 JN.1 和 KP.3.3。值得注意的是,JN.1 菌株在印度一直持续到 2024 年。巴基斯坦的基因组替换率为 0.467E-04(95CI:3.29E-04-6.04E-04),与美国、英国和法国的基因组替换率相似。法国,但高于印度。巴基斯坦的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 平均位置熵较高,为 0.0324(其他国家为 0.01-0.013)。 [10.1007/s42770-026-02147-9]
VYD222 表现出对多种新兴 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体(包括 XFG 变体)的有效中和作用。结构分析显示,VYD222 在 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体中容纳 突变,这些变体逃避了 FDA 批准的其他抗体,特别是那些出现在互补位接触残基之外的第二个外壳中的抗体。 [10.1371/journal.ppat.1014613]
与祖先病毒株 P0 相比,SARS-CoV-2HA P16 会导致更严重的疾病,临床评分明显更高、病毒负荷更高、体重减轻更多、细胞因子风暴显着和肺部损伤明显。 [10.1080/22221751.2026.2760598]
该小组应用于新兴变体,提供了对最近抗原 进化 的机制见解,强调了改变的受体结合结构域构象的潜在作用,并揭示了 JN.1 衍生谱系和 BA.3.2 谱系之间抗体逃避特征的明显差异。 [10.1016/j.celrep.2026.118355]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.headline_en: Recent Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 literature
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Nebulised SNG001 was safe and associated with a reduction in COVID-19-related hospital admission. [10.1080/25310429.2026.2765991]

In Pakistan, XBB.1 and its subvariants were predominant in 2023 and JN.1 and its subvariants persisted through 2024. Whilst, variants KP.2, LB.1, and LA.1 emerging by mid-2024, JN.1 remained dominant. In contrast, SARS-CoV-2 in US, UK and France showed XBB.1.5 transitioned to JN.1 and KP.3.3 by September 2024. [10.1007/s42770-026-02147-9]
VYD222 demonstrated potent neutralization against a broad range of emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants, including the XFG variant. [10.1371/journal.ppat.1014613]

Compared to the ancestral virus strain P0, SARS-CoV-2HA P16 causes more severe disease with significantly higher clinical scores, higher viral burden, more weight loss, prominent cytokine storm, and significant pulmonary injury. [10.1080/22221751.2026.2760598]

The panel was applied to emerging variants, providing mechanistic insight into recent antigenic evolution, highlighting the potential role of altered receptor-binding domain conformation, and revealing clear differences in antibody-evasion profiles between JN.1-derived lineages and BA.3.2 lineages. [10.1016/j.celrep.2026.118355]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The direction of this week's research is defined by the clinical, epidemiological, ecological, diagnostic and molecular topics actually represented by the eligible publications.
literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.
brief_items_zh: 本期SARS-CoV-2研究集中呈现以下进展。

在巴基斯坦,XBB.1 及其子变体在 2023 年占主导地位,JN.1 及其子变体持续到 2024 年。虽然到 2024 年中期出现了 KP.2、LB.1 和 LA.1 变体,但 JN.1 仍然占主导地位。相比之下,美国、英国和法国的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 显示,到 2024 年 9 月,XBB.1.5 转变为 JN.1 和 KP.3.3。值得注意的是,JN.1 菌株在印度一直持续到 2024 年。巴基斯坦的基因组替换率为 0.467E-04(95CI:3.29E-04-6.04E-04),与美国、英国和法国的基因组替换率相似。法国,但高于印度。巴基斯坦的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 平均位置熵较高,为 0.0324(其他国家为 0.01-0.013)。
VYD222 表现出对多种新兴 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体(包括 XFG 变体)的有效中和作用。结构分析显示,VYD222 在 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体中容纳 突变,这些变体逃避了 FDA 批准的其他抗体,特别是那些出现在互补位接触残基之外的第二个外壳中的抗体。
与祖先病毒株 P0 相比,SARS-CoV-2HA P16 会导致更严重的疾病,临床评分明显更高、病毒负荷更高、体重减轻更多、细胞因子风暴显着和肺部损伤明显。 [10.1080/22221751.2026.2760598]。
该小组应用于新兴变体,提供了对最近抗原 进化 的机制见解,强调了改变的受体结合结构域构象的潜在作用,并揭示了 JN.1 衍生谱系和 BA.3.2 谱系之间抗体逃避特征的明显差异。 [10.1016/j.celrep.2026.118355]。
brief_items_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
Nebulised SNG001 was safe and associated with a reduction in COVID-19-related hospital admission. [10.1080/25310429.2026.2765991].

In Pakistan, XBB.1 and its subvariants were predominant in 2023 and JN.1 and its subvariants persisted through 2024. Whilst, variants KP.2, LB.1, and LA.1 emerging by mid-2024, JN.1 remained dominant.
VYD222 demonstrated potent neutralization against a broad range of emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants, including the XFG variant. [10.1371/journal.ppat.1014613].

Compared to the ancestral virus strain P0, SARS-CoV-2HA P16 causes more severe disease with significantly higher clinical scores, higher viral burden, more weight loss, prominent cytokine storm, and significant pulmonary injury.

papers.title: Nebulized interferon-β1a (SNG001) in COVID-19 patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to determine the efficacy of nebulised interferon-β1a (SNG001) in patients with Coronavirus disease-2019 (COVID-19). METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and clinicaltrials.gov, without language restrictions. Studies were searched up to November 2025. Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) on treatment of COVID-19 with SNG001, compared with placebo or standard of care, were reviewed. Data were analysed using the RevMan Version 5.1 (The Cochrane Collaboration). Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for dichotomous outcomes. RESULTS: Four RCTs (enrolling 1055 participants) met the inclusion criteria. The proportion of patients with hospitalisations (data extracted from two RCTs) (RR 0.16, 95% CI 0.03 to 0.88), and serious adverse events (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.47 to 0.90) were significantly fewer in SNG001 groups. There was no statistically significant difference in all-cause mortality (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.37 to 1.39), patients non-recovery at day 28 (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.65 to 1.17), and adverse event (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.04) between the two groups. CONCLUSIONS: Nebulised SNG001 was safe and associated with a reduction in COVID-19-related hospital admission. SNG001 shows a potential benefit for outpatients with COVID-19, but it requires larger clinical trials for future validations, particularly in vaccinated and previously infected populations.

papers.title_zh: Nebulized interferon-β1a (SNG001) in COVID-19 patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to determine the efficacy of nebulised interferon-β1a (SNG001) in patients with Coronavirus disease-2019 (COVID-19). METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and clinicaltrials.gov, without language restrictions. Studies were searched up to November 2025. Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) on treatment of COVID-19 with SNG001, compared with placebo or standard of care, were reviewed. Data were analysed using the RevMan Version 5.1 (The Cochrane Collaboration). Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for dichotomous outcomes. RESULTS: Four RCTs (enrolling 1055 participants) met the inclusion criteria. The proportion of patients with hospitalisations (data extracted from two RCTs) (RR 0.16, 95% CI 0.03 to 0.88), and serious adverse events (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.47 to 0.90) were significantly fewer in SNG001 groups. There was no statistically significant difference in all-cause mortality (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.37 to 1.39), patients non-recovery at day 28 (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.65 to 1.17), and adverse event (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.04) between the two groups. CONCLUSIONS: Nebulised SNG001 was safe and associated with a reduction in COVID-19-related hospital admission. SNG001 shows a potential benefit for outpatients with COVID-19, but it requires larger clinical trials for future validations, particularly in vaccinated and previously infected populations.

papers.title: Retrospective analysis of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron strains (2023 to 2024) from Pakistan reveals differential phylogenetic diversity across genomes compared with other countries
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variants continued to emerge globally in 2023 and 2024 however, genomic epidemiology from Pakistan has been limited. We compared Omicron variants in Pakistan by studying phylogenetic diversity and entropy across genomes compared with isolates from Western countries USA, UK and France, as well as neighbouring India. METHODS: We studied SARS-CoV-2 genomes collected between January 2023 and September 2024. For Pakistan, we also focused on RT-PCR positive samples from Aga Khan University Hospital. Statistical analyses identified P value < 0.05 as considered significant. Genome-based lineages were assigned using Pangolin v4.4 pangoLEARN with clade assignment using Nextclade v3.5.0. Sequences were aligned using MAFFT v7.505 and a maximum-likelihood phylogenetic tree was constructed with IQ-TREE v2.2.0. Substitution rates and Shannon genomic entropy was determined. RESULTS: In Pakistan, XBB.1 and its subvariants were predominant in 2023 and JN.1 and its subvariants persisted through 2024. Whilst, variants KP.2, LB.1, and LA.1 emerging by mid-2024, JN.1 remained dominant. In contrast, SARS-CoV-2 in US, UK and France showed XBB.1.5 transition​ed to JN.1 and KP.3.3 by September 2024. Notably, JN.1 strains persisted in India until 2024. Genomic substitution rates in Pakistan at 0.467E-04 (95CI: 3.29E-04-6.04E-04) were similar compared with those from USA, UK and France, but higher than those from India. SARS-CoV-2 mean positional entropy in Pakistan at 0.0324 was higher (other countries 0.01-0.013). CONCLUSIONS: We describe Omicron diversity in Pakistan with persistence of XBB and JN.1 lineage strains into 2024. These finding provide insights into SARS-CoV-2 genomic evolution. ​The relatively small genomic sequences available limits the comparison with substitution rates between global strains. Expanded surveillance is required to understand local transmission of pandemic strains.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Omicron 变体在 2023 年和 2024 年继续在全球出现,但来自巴基斯坦的基因组 流行病学 受到限制。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们通过研究 基因组 的系统发育多样性和熵,将巴基斯坦的 Omicron 变异与来自西方国家美国、英国和法国以及邻国印度的分离株进行比较。
elements_zh.methods: 我们研究了 2023 年 1 月至 2024 年 9 月期间收集的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 基因组。对于巴基斯坦,我们还重点关注了阿迦汗大学医院的 RT-PCR 阳性样本。统计分析确定 P 值 < 0.05 被认为具有显着性。使用 Pangolin v4.4 pangoLEARN 分配基于 基因组 的谱系,并使用 Nextclade v3.5.0 进行分支分配。使用 MAFFT v7.505 比对序列,并使用 IQ-TREE v2.2.0 构建最大似然系统发育树。确定替代率和香农基因组熵。
elements_zh.main_results: 在巴基斯坦,XBB.1 及其子变体在 2023 年占主导地位,JN.1 及其子变体持续到 2024 年。虽然到 2024 年中期出现了 KP.2、LB.1 和 LA.1 变体,但 JN.1 仍然占主导地位。相比之下,美国、英国和法国的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 显示,到 2024 年 9 月,XBB.1.5 转变为 JN.1 和 KP.3.3。值得注意的是,JN.1 菌株在印度一直持续到 2024 年。巴基斯坦的基因组替换率为 0.467E-04(95CI:3.29E-04-6.04E-04),与美国、英国和法国的基因组替换率相似。法国,但高于印度。巴基斯坦的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 平均位置熵较高,为 0.0324(其他国家为 0.01-0.013)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 我们描述了巴基斯坦的 Omicron 多样性,XBB 和 JN.1 谱系菌株的持续存在直至 2024 年。这些发现提供了对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 基因组 进化 的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 需要扩展 监测 来了解流行毒株的本地 传播。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 可用的基因组序列相对较小,限制了全球菌株之间替代率的比较。

papers.title: A monoclonal antibody panel to track antigenic evolution of SARS-CoV-2 JN.1 subvariants
papers.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 continues to evolve, generating successive variants with enhanced resistance to antibody-mediated neutralization. However, many existing monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) were derived from ancestral or early Omicron strains and have lost activity against recent variants, limiting their ability to resolve the antigenic effects of mutations arising in emerging lineages. Here, we generated a mAb panel by immunizing naive, unimprinted VelocImmune mice with the KP.3.1.1 spike, and isolated and characterized 11 human neutralizing antibodies targeting diverse epitopes of evolved variants. We then integrated these antibodies with characterized mAbs to establish a toolbox for profiling antigenic evolution among emerging variants. Application of this panel to emerging variants provided mechanistic insight into recent antigenic evolution, highlighting the potential role of altered receptor-binding domain conformation. Our data also revealed clear differences in antibody-evasion profiles between JN.1-derived lineages and BA.3.2 lineages. Together, our findings establish an updated mAb panel for monitoring antigenic evolution of JN.1 subvariants.

papers.title_zh: 用于追踪 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 JN.1 亚变体的抗原 进化 的单克隆抗体组合
papers.source_body_en: SARS-CoV-2 continues to evolve, generating successive variants with enhanced resistance to antibody-mediated neutralization. However, many existing monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) were derived from ancestral or early Omicron strains and have lost activity against recent variants, limiting their ability to resolve the antigenic effects of mutations arising in emerging lineages. Here, we generated a mAb panel by immunizing naive, unimprinted VelocImmune mice with the KP.3.1.1 spike, and isolated and characterized 11 human neutralizing antibodies targeting diverse epitopes of evolved variants. We then integrated these antibodies with characterized mAbs to establish a toolbox for profiling antigenic evolution among emerging variants. Application of this panel to emerging variants provided mechanistic insight into recent antigenic evolution, highlighting the potential role of altered receptor-binding domain conformation. Our data also revealed clear differences in antibody-evasion profiles between JN.1-derived lineages and BA.3.2 lineages. Together, our findings establish an updated mAb panel for monitoring antigenic evolution of JN.1 subvariants.

papers.title: Structural and functional analysis of VYD222: A broadly neutralizing antibody against SARS-CoV-2 variants.
papers.abstract: Extensive mutations in SARS-CoV-2 spike protein have rendered most therapeutic monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) ineffective. However, here we describe how VYD222 (pemivibart), a human mAb re-engineered from ADG20 (adintrevimab) exhibits substantially improved neutralization potency and breadth against SARS-CoV-2 variants despite substantial virus evolution. VYD222 received FDA Emergency Use Authorization for pre-exposure prophylaxis of COVID-19 in certain immunocompromised adults and adolescents. Here we show potent neutralization of this antibody against a broad range of emerging variants, including the recently dominant XFG. X-ray crystal structures of VYD222 in complex with the receptor-binding domains of prototype SARS-CoV-2 and Omicron BA.5 demonstrate the molecular basis of how VYD222 accommodates the mutations in SARS-CoV-2 variants that escape other previous FDA-approved antibodies. Notably, many of the mutations between ADG20 and VYD222 occur in the second shell outside the paratope contact residues. Deep mutational scanning indicates that SARS-CoV-2's ability to escape VYD222 is constrained by structural compatibility and the need to maintain receptor binding. These findings provide crucial insights into the escape-resistant neutralization of VYD222 against a broad panel of clinically relevant SARS-CoV-2 variants and offer valuable guidance for risk assessment of emergent variants.

papers.title: [Dynamics of behavioral factors and attitudes toward vaccination in moscow during the COVID-19 pandemic: from the acute phase to adaptation].
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The transition of the COVID-19 pandemic from the acute phase to adaptation was accompanied by changes in preventive behavior, institutional trust, emotional state and attitudes toward vaccination. OBJECTIVE: To analyze the dynamics of awareness, preventive behavior, trust, emotional state and attitudes toward vaccination among Moscow residents in 2021 compared with 2020. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The survey tool was developed by the WHO Regional Office for Europe with support from the University of Erfurt and adapted to the Moscow context. CATI was conducted using a stratified dual-frame sample. The article analyzes the 4th and 5th survey waves: February 2021 (n = 1038) and July-August 2021 (n = 998). RESULTS: By the 5th wave, adherence to most preventive measures decreased, especially social distancing, limiting contacts and using hand sanitizers. The proportion not wearing gloves increased sharply after the requirement was lifted. The mean self-assessment of emotional state decreased to 3.47 points; institutional assessments declined and vaccination attitudes became more polarized. CONCLUSIONS: Public health strategies should combine consistent scientific communication, targeted work with vaccine-hesitant groups and horizontal trust.

papers.title: Echoes of infection: viral persistence, immune activation, and histopathological changes in long COVID: a systematic review
papers.abstract: Long COVID, or post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC), affects an estimated 10–20% of individuals following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Despite its substantial global burden, the pathophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This systematic review aimed to synthesize available evidence on viral persistence, immune activation, and histopathological changes across multiple organ systems, drawing from studies of individuals with Long COVID as well as broader post-acute cohorts, autopsy investigations, and case-based reports relevant to Long COVID pathophysiology. Following PRISMA guidelines and holding a PROSPERO registration (CRD420261403869), a systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, and Cochrane CENTRAL. Eligible reports were stratified as (A) symptom-defined Long COVID assessed at or after 12 weeks, (B) post-acute or mixed populations without a consistently confirmed Long COVID definition or timing, (C) autopsy studies, and (D) isolated case/fetal reports. Findings were synthesized narratively by specimen, assay target, and unit of analysis. JBI checklists were used for item-level appraisal, not as certainty-of-evidence ratings. Forty-five reports were included: 16 in stratum A, 23 in stratum B, three autopsy studies, and three isolated case/fetal reports. SARS-CoV-2 genomic RNA, viral proteins, and markers compatible with recent viral activity were reported in selected tissue and blood compartments, but detection varied with population selection, timing, specimen, and assay. No included study established replication competence by recovery of infectious virus. Histopathological abnormalities included inflammatory infiltrates, fibrosis, and vascular injury; however, causal attribution to Long COVID was limited by acute disease severity, biopsy indication, comorbidity, and incomplete comparator data. A single participant total was not reported because of overlapping cohorts, repeated sampling, and outcome-specific denominators. The review supports biological heterogeneity after SARS-CoV-2 infection, including residual viral material, immune dysregulation, vascular injury, and maladaptive tissue repair. Organ-specific prevalence, a hierarchy of tissue tropism, replication-competent reservoirs, and superiority of antiviral or immunomodulatory treatment remain undefined. Standardized Long COVID definitions, representative cohorts, validated assays, appropriate comparators, and longitudinal studies linking biological markers to clinical outcomes are required.

It synthesizes evidence from 45 studies, including symptom-defined Long COVID cohorts, post-acute populations, autopsy investigations, and case-based reports. Additionally, the review calls for improved methodologies, including validated assays and longitudinal studies, to better understand Long COVID's biological underpinnings and clinical outcomes.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 长新冠 或 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 (PASC) 的急性后遗症影响 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染后估计 10-20% 的个体。本系统综述旨在综合关于跨多个器官系统的病毒持久性、免疫激活和组织病理学变化的现有证据,借鉴对 长新冠 个体的研究以及更广泛的急性后 队列研究、尸检调查和与 长新冠 病理生理学相关的基于病例的报告。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 遵循 PRISMA 指南并持有 PROSPERO 注册 (CRD420261403869),在 PubMed、Scopus、EMBASE 和 Cochrane CENTRAL 上进行了系统文献检索。合格的报告被分层为(A)在12周或之后评估的症状定义的长新冠,(B)没有一致确认的长新冠定义或时间的急性后或混合人群,(C)尸检研究,以及(D)孤立的病例/胎儿报告。研究结果按样本、分析目标和分析单位进行叙述性综合。JBI 检查表用于项目级评估,而不是证据确定性评级。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述支持 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染后的生物异质性,包括残留病毒物质、免疫失调、血管损伤和适应不良组织修复。在选定的组织和血液隔室中报告了 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 基因组 RNA、病毒蛋白和与近期病毒活性兼容的标记物,但检测结果因群体选择、时间、标本和测定而异。

papers.title: A dose of reality: autodisable syringe supply challenges in the COVID-19 immunization response.
papers.abstract: Autodisable (AD) syringes are vital for safe immunization, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, as they prevent reuse and reduce the risk of disease transmission. Prior to the COVID-19 pandemic, global supply was stable and met routine immunization needs. The pandemic, however, highlighted coordination challenges in aligning vaccine and injection device supply chains. The rapid rollout of COVID-19 vaccines led to a surge in demand for AD syringes, including those with nonstandard dose volumes, which required new product development and matching of syringes to specific vaccines-a synchronization that is typically not needed. Limited early information on COVID-19 vaccine dose volume specifications, long lead times, and lack of coordination between vaccine and syringe stakeholders created forecasting difficulties. Procurement agencies faced increased costs and logistical constraints and had to quickly adapt contracts and supply strategies. Although manufacturing capacity expanded, syringe shortages still emerged, increasing the risk of dosing errors and placing additional strain on health systems. As demand later declined, oversupply and market instability followed, prompting contract adjustments. This paper incorporates lessons learned from the COVID-19 response and emphasizes that syringes must not be an afterthought in immunization planning for both future outbreak preparedness and routine immunization efforts. It also outlines key strategies for strengthening syringe market resilience.

papers.title: Modelling severe COVID-19 by adaptation of SARS-CoV-2 in Syrian hamsters.
papers.abstract: While most patients infected with recent Omicron subvariants develop milder disease than those infected with preceding SARS-CoV-2 strains, some patients remain susceptible to developing severe disease and/or long-term complications. The pathogenesis of and optimal countermeasures for severe COVID-19 remain incompletely understood. Readily available small animal models closely mimicking severe COVID-19 are lacking. We have previously established a Syrian hamster model for COVID-19 that mimics mild-to-moderate disease in humans. In this study, we established a new Syrian hamster model resembling severe COVID-19 using a hamster-adapted SARS-CoV-2 (SARS-CoV-2HA) obtained through serial passage. Compared to the ancestral virus strain P0, SARS-CoV-2HA P16 causes more severe disease with significantly higher clinical scores, higher viral burden, more weight loss, prominent cytokine storm, and significant pulmonary injury. Age and sex are key factors influencing disease severity in this model. Comparing SARS-CoV-2HA P16 and P0, N_S194L was identified as a key adaptive mutation that enhances the antagonistic effect of SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein and viral replication. Using this new SARS-CoV-2HA P16 model, we showed that nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir were effective in improving the clinical and virological parameters of hamsters with severe COVID-19. This new model serves as a robust platform for investigating the pathogenesis of and countermeasures for severe COVID-19.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The pathogenesis of and optimal countermeasures for severe COVID-19 remain incompletely understood. Readily available small animal models closely mimicking severe COVID-19 are lacking.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a Syrian hamster model that closely mimics severe COVID-19, addressing the lack of such models. The researchers adapted SARS-CoV-2 through serial passage to create a strain (SARS-CoV-2HA P16) that induced more severe disease in hamsters compared to the ancestral strain P0, as evidenced by higher clinical scores, viral burden, weight loss, cytokine storm, and pulmonary injury. The model demonstrated the effectiveness of nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir in improving clinical and virological outcomes in severe cases. The study highlights the importance of age and sex in disease severity and provides a valuable platform for further research on severe COVID-19 pathogenesis and countermeasures. However, the findings are limited to the hamster model and may not fully translate to human conditions.

papers.title: Time-Dependent Activity of SARS-CoV-2 Mpro Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic led to the rapid development of vaccines and antiviral drugs to prevent severe disease and death. Several drugs that inhibit the essential main viral protease Mpro are in clinical use (Voget R, Gutschow M. Early Kinetic Characterization of SARS-CoV-2 Main Protease Inhibitors: A Review and Guidance for Biochemical Assessments. 2026;65:860-81.) and additional Mpro inhibitors are being developed to address drug-resistance and novel emergent coronaviruses. Early drug discovery and development has primarily used non-cell-based biochemical assays to characterize the pharmacokinetic properties of drug candidates (Tonge PJ. Drug-target kinetics in drug discovery. Because drugs that remain bound to the target may have prolonged activity following drug elimination enabling dose frequency to be reduced, we evaluated the relationship between target residence time and antiviral activity of four Mpro inhibitors with different mechanisms of action. This included the irreversible inhibitor N3, the noncovalent inhibitor ensitrelvir, which had a residence time of 2.4 min, and the reversible covalent inhibitors 13b and nirmatrelvir, which had residence times of 19 and 23.3 min, respectively. To correlate the in vitro residence times with time-dependent antiviral activity, we performed washout experiments with Vero-E6 cells infected with SARS-CoV-2. While all the compounds inhibited viral RNA production, ensitrelvir with the shortest residence time was significantly less active than the other compounds following washout. The intracellular washout experiments confirmed that ensitrelvir exhibited a shorter residence time in SARS-CoV-2-infected cells, falling below the functional lifespan of nascent viral replicase/transcriptase complexes.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study focuses on SARS-CoV-2 and evaluates the relationship between the target residence time of four Mpro inhibitors and their antiviral activity. The central question is whether the duration of drug-target binding influences the effectiveness of these inhibitors against SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis of the pharmacokinetic properties of Mpro inhibitors. It includes in vitro washout experiments with Vero-E6 cells infected with SARS-CoV-2 to correlate residence time with antiviral activity. The evidence is derived from biochemical assays and experimental data on drug-target interactions.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study concludes that the residence time of Mpro inhibitors in SARS-CoV-2-infected cells is associated with their antiviral activity. Specifically, compounds with longer residence times, such as nirmatrelvir, showed greater antiviral efficacy compared to ensitrelvir, which had the shortest residence time and was less active post-washout.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The evidence highlights a potential limitation in early drug discovery methods, which primarily used non-cell-based assays. This may have led to an incomplete understanding of in vivo drug behavior. Additionally, the study does not address the long-term effects of these inhibitors or their performance against emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings suggest that future drug development should prioritize compounds with longer target residence times to enhance antiviral efficacy. There is also a need for more comprehensive in vitro and in vivo studies to evaluate the effectiveness of Mpro inhibitors against new SARS-CoV-2 variants and to refine dosing strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the relationship between the target residence time of four SARS-CoV-2 Mpro inhibitors and their antiviral activity. The study uses in vitro washout experiments with Vero-E6 cells to demonstrate that compounds with longer residence times, such as nirmatrelvir, exhibit greater antiviral efficacy compared to ensitrelvir, which had the shortest residence time and was less active post-washout. The evidence underscores the importance of residence time in determining drug effectiveness and highlights the need for more in vivo studies to assess performance against emerging variants. The findings suggest that future drug development should focus on improving residence time to optimize antiviral activity and dosing strategies.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该研究重点关注严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2,评估四种Mpro抑制剂的目标停留时间与其抗病毒药物活性之间的关系。核心问题是药物靶标结合的持续时间是否会影响这些抑制剂对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的有效性。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对 Mpro 抑制剂的药代动力学特性的系统分析。它包括用感染 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的 Vero-E6 细胞进行体外冲洗实验,以将停留时间与 抗病毒药物 活性相关联。证据来自生化测定和药物-靶标相互作用的实验数据。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 研究得出结论,Mpro 抑制剂在 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染细胞中的停留时间与其 抗病毒药物 活性相关。具体而言,与滞留时间最短且清洗后活性较低的恩斯特韦相比,滞留时间较长的化合物(例如 nirmatrelvir)显示出更高的 抗病毒药物 功效。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 这些证据凸显了早期药物发现方法的潜在局限性,这些方法主要使用非细胞分析。这可能导致对体内药物行为的不完全理解。此外,该研究并未解决这些抑制剂的长期影响或其​​针对新兴 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体的性能。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 研究结果表明,未来的药物开发应优先考虑目标停留时间较长的化合物,以增强 抗病毒药物 的疗效。还需要更全面的体外和体内研究来评估 Mpro 抑制剂对新 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体的有效性并完善给药策略。

papers.abstract_zh: 新型冠状病毒感染 大流行导致了 疫苗 和 抗病毒药物 药物的快速开发,以预防严重疾病和死亡。抑制重要的主要病毒蛋白酶 Mpro 的几种药物已投入临床使用(Voget R,Gutschow M. 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Main Protease Inhibitors Early Kinetic Characterization of 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Main Protease Inhibitors: A Review and Guidance for Biochemical Assessments. 2026;65:860-81.),并且正在开发其他 Mpro 抑制剂以解决耐药性和新型冠状病毒的问题。早期药物发现和开发主要使用非细胞生化测定来表征候选药物的药代动力学特性(Tonge PJ。药物发现中的药物靶标动力学。由于药物消除后仍与靶标结合的药物可能具有延长的活性,从而使剂量频率降低,因此我们评估了四种具有不同作用机制的 Mpro 抑制剂的靶标停留时间与 抗病毒药物 活性之间的关系。这包括不可逆抑制剂 N3、非共价抑制剂 ensitrelvir、其滞留时间为 2.4 分钟,可逆共价抑制剂 13b 和 nirmatrelvir 的滞留时间分别为 19 和 23.3 分钟。为了将体外滞留时间与时间依赖性 抗病毒药物 活性相关联,我们用 抗病毒药物 感染的 Vero-E6 细胞进行了洗脱实验,虽然所有化合物均抑制病毒 RNA 产生,但滞留时间最短的是 ensitrelvir。细胞内清除实验证实,ensitrelvir 在 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染的细胞中的停留时间明显低于其他化合物,低于新生病毒复制酶/转录酶复合物的功能寿命。

analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 这些证据凸显了早期药物发现方法的潜在局限性,这些方法主要使用非细胞分析。这可能导致对体内药物行为的不完全理解。此外,该研究并未解决这些抑制剂的长期影响或其​​针对新兴 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体的性能。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 研究结果表明,未来的药物开发应优先考虑目标停留时间较长的化合物,以增强 抗病毒药物 的疗效。还需要更全面的体外和体内研究来评估 Mpro 抑制剂对新 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体的有效性并完善给药策略。

papers.title: SARS-CoV-2 antibody landscape following multiple vaccinations and infections during Omicron period
papers.abstract: Background: Repeated COVID-19 vaccination effects on the immunogenicity, breadth, and durability of antibody responses across antigenically distinct SARS-CoV-2 variants remain incompletely understood. Method: Participants receiving >= five COVID-19 vaccine doses 2020-2025 were selected from a prospective cohort in Michigan. Serum IgG, IgM, and ACE2 percent inhibition were measured using multiplex assays. Baseline-adjusted immunogenicity, cross-reactivity, and formulation-specific antibody durability were evaluated using regression models. Result: Twenty-one participants were included (median: seven vaccine doses). For every two-fold increase in pre-vaccination IgG concentration, post-vaccination fold-rise was 34% (95% CI: 16%-48%), 43% (95% CI: 15%-62%), and 55% (95% CI: 21%-75%) lower following monovalent, bivalent, and 2023-24 vaccination, while baseline-adjusted immunogenicity showed no significant trends across successive vaccines. Antibody landscapes demonstrated broad cross-reactivity against ancestral and Omicron variants, with similar strain-specific IgG changes across ancestral, vaccine-matched, and antigenically distant strains, but greater heterogeneity in ACE2 inhibition. Formulation-specific waning models showed significant IgG declines following monovalent and bivalent vaccination (beta = -1.03, 95% CI: -1.51 to -0.55; P<0.001 and -1.00 , 95% CI: -1.71 to -0.30; P=0.007, respectively) and ACE2 inhibition declines following monovalent vaccination, while other formulations showed less consistent changes. Despite waning, antibody levels generally remained relatively high across variants up to 300 days post-vaccination, with formulation-specific differences in durability. Conclusion: Repeated COVID-19 vaccination maintained baseline-adjusted immunogenicity and broad cross-reactive antibody responses, with formulation-specific differences in durability. Higher baseline immunity was associated with smaller post-vaccination increases, suggesting repeated boosting continues to reinforce humoral immunity despite increasingly complex immune histories.

papers.source_body_en: Background: Repeated COVID-19 vaccination effects on the immunogenicity, breadth, and durability of antibody responses across antigenically distinct SARS-CoV-2 variants remain incompletely understood. Method: Participants receiving >= five COVID-19 vaccine doses 2020-2025 were selected from a prospective cohort in Michigan. Serum IgG, IgM, and ACE2 percent inhibition were measured using multiplex assays. Baseline-adjusted immunogenicity, cross-reactivity, and formulation-specific antibody durability were evaluated using regression models. Result: Twenty-one participants were included (median: seven vaccine doses). For every two-fold increase in pre-vaccination IgG concentration, post-vaccination fold-rise was 34% (95% CI: 16%-48%), 43% (95% CI: 15%-62%), and 55% (95% CI: 21%-75%) lower following monovalent, bivalent, and 2023-24 vaccination, while baseline-adjusted immunogenicity showed no significant trends across successive vaccines. Antibody landscapes demonstrated broad cross-reactivity against ancestral and Omicron variants, with similar strain-specific IgG changes across ancestral, vaccine-matched, and antigenically distant strains, but greater heterogeneity in ACE2 inhibition. Formulation-specific waning models showed significant IgG declines following monovalent and bivalent vaccination (beta = -1.03, 95% CI: -1.51 to -0.55; P<0.001 and -1.00 , 95% CI: -1.71 to -0.30; P=0.007, respectively) and ACE2 inhibition declines following monovalent vaccination, while other formulations showed less consistent changes. Despite waning, antibody levels generally remained relatively high across variants up to 300 days post-vaccination, with formulation-specific differences in durability. Conclusion: Repeated COVID-19 vaccination maintained baseline-adjusted immunogenicity and broad cross-reactive antibody responses, with formulation-specific differences in durability. Higher baseline immunity was associated with smaller post-vaccination increases, suggesting repeated boosting continues to reinforce humoral immunity despite increasingly complex immune histories.

papers.title: Misperceived norms and willingness to get a COVID-19 vaccine: a whole-population study of adults in rural Uganda.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Perceptions about others' willingness to get vaccinated for COVID-19 are understudied in HIV-endemic settings. Perceived social norms influence engagement in other protective behaviors. Information about COVID-19 vaccine norms could inform future HIV vaccination efforts. METHODS: All adults across 8 villages in Uganda completed a survey in 2021-2022. Participants reported personal willingness to take a COVID-19 vaccine (definitely yes vs any hesitance) and estimated how many village adults would take a COVID-19 vaccine ("all or almost all," "more than half," "less than half," "very few or no one," "do not know"). Participants also reported COVID-19 related beliefs, whether they knew someone who had COVID-19, personal HIV status, and sociodemographic characteristics. A multivariable Poisson regression model estimated associations between perceptions about others' willingness to get a vaccine and personal willingness to get a vaccine. RESULTS: Among 1561 participants (>90% response rate), 1163 (75%) were willing to get a COVID-19 vaccine. One in three vaccine-hesitant participants and 1 in 10 vaccine-willing participants incorrectly thought most adults in their village would not get vaccinated. Compared to participants who thought more than half of villagers were willing to get vaccinated, those who mistakenly thought fewer than half (adjusted relative risk [aRR] = 0.81; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.70-0.94) or few to none (aRR = 0.65; 95% CI: 0.50-0.85) were willing were less likely to report willingness themselves. CONCLUSIONS: Overall, one-fifth of adults mistakenly thought most other villagers were unwilling to get vaccinated. Adults with this misperception were less willing to get a COVID-19 vaccine themselves. Strategies that provide information about vaccine effectiveness and communicate that most adults are willing to get vaccinated may increase uptake. Changing perceived norms about vaccine uptake may also foster conversations about accessing vaccines and reduce vaccine-related stigma, important considerations with an HIV vaccine on the horizon.

papers.title_zh: Misperceived norms and willingness to get a COVID-19 vaccine: a whole-population study of adults in rural Uganda.
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Perceptions about others' willingness to get vaccinated for COVID-19 are understudied in HIV-endemic settings. Perceived social norms influence engagement in other protective behaviors. Information about COVID-19 vaccine norms could inform future HIV vaccination efforts. METHODS: All adults across 8 villages in Uganda completed a survey in 2021-2022. Participants reported personal willingness to take a COVID-19 vaccine (definitely yes vs any hesitance) and estimated how many village adults would take a COVID-19 vaccine ("all or almost all," "more than half," "less than half," "very few or no one," "do not know"). Participants also reported COVID-19 related beliefs, whether they knew someone who had COVID-19, personal HIV status, and sociodemographic characteristics. A multivariable Poisson regression model estimated associations between perceptions about others' willingness to get a vaccine and personal willingness to get a vaccine. RESULTS: Among 1561 participants (>90% response rate), 1163 (75%) were willing to get a COVID-19 vaccine. One in three vaccine-hesitant participants and 1 in 10 vaccine-willing participants incorrectly thought most adults in their village would not get vaccinated. Compared to participants who thought more than half of villagers were willing to get vaccinated, those who mistakenly thought fewer than half (adjusted relative risk [aRR] = 0.81; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.70-0.94) or few to none (aRR = 0.65; 95% CI: 0.50-0.85) were willing were less likely to report willingness themselves. CONCLUSIONS: Overall, one-fifth of adults mistakenly thought most other villagers were unwilling to get vaccinated. Adults with this misperception were less willing to get a COVID-19 vaccine themselves. Strategies that provide information about vaccine effectiveness and communicate that most adults are willing to get vaccinated may increase uptake. Changing perceived norms about vaccine uptake may also foster conversations about accessing vaccines and reduce vaccine-related stigma, important considerations with an HIV vaccine on the horizon.

papers.title: A decoupled ensemble framework for real-time nowcasting of COVID-19 case numbers and transmission dynamics.
papers.abstract: Timely monitoring of epidemics such as SARS-CoV-2 transmission is essential for guiding public health and social measures, yet real-time estimation of the time-varying effective reproductive number ( R t ) from case data suffers from right-censoring bias, systematically underestimating recent R t values and requiring 7-14 days of additional data to stabilize. To address this limitation, we developed and evaluated a three-step framework that decouples case forecasting from R t estimation. Daily PCR-confirmed case counts are first forecast up to 14 days ahead using an ensemble of 10 statistical, machine learning and deep learning models. Forecasted cases are then deconvolved to reconstruct infection timelines, from which R t is estimated for up to 7 days ahead. This approach mitigates right-censoring artefacts by generating R t estimates from projected rather than truncated case data. We applied this framework to Hong Kong's Omicron outbreaks (February to December 2022), incorporating 15 epidemiological, meteorological, air pollution and policy-related predictors. An unweighted ensemble of top-performing models substantially improved forecast accuracy, reducing the root mean square error and the mean absolute percentage error by 10 and 9% for case numbers and by 38 and 34% for R t . By separating predictive modelling from epidemiological inference, this framework enables accurate real-time monitoring of epidemic burden and transmission dynamics to support timely public health decision-making.

papers.title_zh: A decoupled ensemble framework for real-time nowcasting of COVID-19 case numbers and transmission dynamics.
papers.source_body_en: Timely monitoring of epidemics such as SARS-CoV-2 transmission is essential for guiding public health and social measures, yet real-time estimation of the time-varying effective reproductive number ( R t ) from case data suffers from right-censoring bias, systematically underestimating recent R t values and requiring 7-14 days of additional data to stabilize. To address this limitation, we developed and evaluated a three-step framework that decouples case forecasting from R t estimation. Daily PCR-confirmed case counts are first forecast up to 14 days ahead using an ensemble of 10 statistical, machine learning and deep learning models. Forecasted cases are then deconvolved to reconstruct infection timelines, from which R t is estimated for up to 7 days ahead. This approach mitigates right-censoring artefacts by generating R t estimates from projected rather than truncated case data. We applied this framework to Hong Kong's Omicron outbreaks (February to December 2022), incorporating 15 epidemiological, meteorological, air pollution and policy-related predictors. An unweighted ensemble of top-performing models substantially improved forecast accuracy, reducing the root mean square error and the mean absolute percentage error by 10 and 9% for case numbers and by 38 and 34% for R t . By separating predictive modelling from epidemiological inference, this framework enables accurate real-time monitoring of epidemic burden and transmission dynamics to support timely public health decision-making.

papers.title: Identification of small-molecule inhibitors of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD–ACE2 interaction by structure- and affinity-based screening
papers.abstract: Abstract The receptor-binding domain (RBD) of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike protein mediates viral entry through its interaction with angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), making it an attractive target for antiviral intervention. However, the broad and relatively shallow ACE2-binding interface presents a challenge for small-molecule inhibitor discovery. In the present study, we explored conserved regions outside the ACE2-binding interface as potential druggable sites for small-molecule inhibitors targeting the SARS-CoV-2 RBD. Structure-based virtual screening was performed using the structure of the SARS-CoV-1 RBD as a structural surrogate, and selected compounds were evaluated using a newly established affinity-based assay on diazirine-modified amorphous carbon plates. Evaluation of 175 virtual hits identified eight RBD-binding compounds. Among them, only RABI-1 inhibited RBD–ACE2 interaction in a Calu-3 cell-based binding assay without affecting ACE2 expression or cell viability. Evaluation of structural analogs of RABI-1 led to the identification of RABI-3, which showed stronger inhibitory activity compared with RABI-1. In addition, RABI-3 inhibited the interaction between ACE2 and RBDs derived from multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants in an AlphaLISA immunoassay and suppressed pseudovirus infection in Calu-3 cells. These findings support the feasibility of targeting regions of the RBD outside the ACE2-binding interface as a strategy for identifying small-molecule inhibitors of SARS-CoV-2 entry.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2 (严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2) 刺突蛋白 的受体结合域 (RBD) 通过与血管紧张素转换酶 2 (ACE2) 相互作用介导病毒进入,使其成为 抗病毒药物 干预的有吸引力的靶点。然而,广泛且相对浅的 ACE2 结合界面对小分子抑制剂的发现提出了挑战。在本研究中,我们探索了 ACE2 结合界面之外的保守区域,作为针对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 RBD 的小分子抑制剂的潜在药物位点。使用 SARS-CoV-1 RBD 的结构作为结构替代物进行基于结构的虚拟筛选,并使用新建立的基于亲和力的测定法在二氮丙啶修饰的无定形碳板上评估选定的化合物。对 175 个虚拟命中的评估确定了 8 种 RBD 结合化合物。其中,在基于 Calu-3 细胞的结合测定中,只有 RABI-1 抑制 RBD-ACE2 相互作用,而不影响 ACE2 表达或细胞活力。对 RABI-1 结构类似物的评估导致了 RABI-3 的鉴定,与 RABI-1 相比,RABI-3 显示出更强的抑制活性。此外,RABI-3 在 AlphaLISA 免疫测定中抑制了 ACE2 和源自多个 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体的 RBD 之间的相互作用,并抑制了 Calu-3 细胞中的假病毒感染。这些发现支持以 ACE2 结合界面之外的 RBD 区域为目标的可行性,作为识别 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 进入的小分子抑制剂的策略。

papers.title: Spatiotemporal analysis of COVID-19 in Japan: The twelve epidemic waves from 2020 to 2025
papers.abstract: Since the first confirmed case of COVID-19 in Japan in January 2020, multiple epidemic waves have emerged under changing legal classifications and public health measures. Although nationwide surveillance data have been continuously available, integrated analyses of temporal and geographic patterns remain limited. This study described the spatiotemporal evolution of COVID-19 in Japan in relation to the timing of major policy, vaccination, variant, and surveillance changes. Weekly prefecture-level case counts from 2020 to 2025 were analyzed using official data from the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, and the epidemic period was divided into early epidemic, expansion, and plateau phases. Three-dimensional log-transformed visualizations were generated to illustrate nationwide temporal and regional trends. We identified twelve epidemic waves. Early outbreaks were localized in densely populated urban areas with low synchrony. During the expansion phase, large nationwide waves occurred in the period when a highly transmissible variant emerged, and peak timing was most closely aligned across prefectures in the 5th and 7th waves. In the plateau phase, following the transition to “Category 5 infectious disease,” reported waves were lower and more prolonged, with smaller differences among prefectures; because these values are based on sentinel reports, they are not directly comparable with earlier phases. Overall, COVID-19 in Japan evolved from localized clusters to synchronized nationwide waves with reduced regional differences across prefectures, suggesting the value of integrated spatiotemporal surveillance frameworks for future pandemic preparedness.

papers.title: Predictors and prevalence of symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing four years after COVID-19: a prospective observational study
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dysfunctional breathing is increasingly recognised among individuals with post-COVID-19 condition (PCC), yet data on long-term prevalence and predictors are scarce. This study assessed the prevalence of symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing, as indicated by elevated Nijmegen questionnaire (NQ) scores, four years after COVID-19 illness in adults with PCC and identified associated factors and baseline predictors by comparing individuals with and without elevated NQ scores. METHOD: In this prospective observational study, adults with PCC, both previously hospitalised and non-hospitalised for COVID-19, were recruited from a specialised post-COVID outpatient clinic. Baseline assessments (2020-2022) were analysed together with data from a digital follow-up survey in 2024. Symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing was defined as a NQ score ≥ 23 at follow-up. Between group differences were examined, and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify associated factors and baseline predictors. RESULTS: Among 288 participants (median follow-up 50 months), 143 (50%) had symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing. These individuals were younger, often female, and more frequently non-hospitalised during acute COVID-19. Baseline predictors included non-hospitalisation, higher dyspnoea severity, lower FEV1, and younger age. At four years, elevated NQ scores (≥ 23) were independently associated with higher dyspnoea severity, greater PCC-symptom burden, depressive symptoms and postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome. Individuals with symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing performed worse in the six-minute walk test, one-minute sit to stand test, and maximal inspiratory pressure test at baseline, whereas lung function did not differ. Patient-reported outcomes were consistently worse compared with those with NQ scores < 23 and improved less over time. CONCLUSION: Half of the individuals with PCC in this cohort reported symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing four years after COVID-19, as indicated by a NQ score ≥ 23. Elevated NQ scores were associated with greater PCC-symptom burden and poorer health outcomes, highlighting their potential clinical relevance in long-term PCC. Future studies should combine patient-reported measures with objective assessment of breathing pattern and ventilatory function.

source_records.abstract: Dysfunctional breathing is increasingly recognised among individuals with post-COVID-19 condition (PCC), yet data on long-term prevalence and predictors are scarce. This study assessed the prevalence of symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing, as indicated by elevated Nijmegen questionnaire (NQ) scores, four years after COVID-19 illness in adults with PCC and identified associated factors and baseline predictors by comparing individuals with and without elevated NQ scores. In this prospective observational study, adults with PCC, both previously hospitalised and non-hospitalised for COVID-19, were recruited from a specialised post-COVID outpatient clinic. Baseline assessments (2020–2022) were analysed together with data from a digital follow-up survey in 2024. Symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing was defined as a NQ score ≥ 23 at follow-up. papers.title: Evolution of the clinical profile and cardiac outcomes of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) across three COVID-19 waves in Central Kerala: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare the clinical profile, laboratory findings, cardiac manifestations, treatment patterns and outcomes of children diagnosed with multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) across the Alpha, Delta and Omicron waves of the COVID-19 pandemic. DESIGN: Cross-sectional observational study. SETTING: A tertiary care teaching hospital in Central Kerala, India. PARTICIPANTS: 95 children fulfilling established diagnostic criteria for MIS-C admitted between November 2020 and December 2022 were included. Patients were categorised into three groups according to the predominant SARS-CoV-2 variant wave: Alpha (wave 1), Delta (wave 2) and Omicron (wave 3). MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Clinical characteristics, laboratory parameters, echocardiographic findings, treatment modalities and markers of disease severity, including duration of hospitalisation, intensive care stay, oxygen requirement, inotropic support and ventilator support. RESULTS: Gastrointestinal symptoms remained the predominant presentation across all three waves, whereas respiratory symptoms increased during the later waves. Mucocutaneous manifestations varied significantly across waves (p=0.02). The duration of hospital stay (p=0.004), duration of fever (p=0.009) and pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels (p=0.003) decreased significantly over successive waves, suggesting reduced overall disease severity. Pericardial effusion also decreased significantly (p=0.002), while the prevalence of left ventricular dysfunction showed a declining trend. In contrast, coronary artery dilatation increased significantly during the Omicron wave (p<0.0001). Oxygen requirement declined significantly in the third wave (p=0.02), whereas intensive care stay, inotropic support and ventilator support did not differ significantly between waves. CONCLUSIONS: The clinical phenotype of MIS-C evolved across successive COVID-19 waves, with evidence of decreasing systemic disease severity but persistent changes in cardiac involvement. The marked increase in coronary artery dilatation during the Omicron wave highlights the importance of continued echocardiographic surveillance and long-term cardiac follow-up, even during clinically milder phases of the pandemic.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study compared the clinical profile and cardiac outcomes of children with MIS-C across three waves of the COVID-19 pandemic in Central Kerala, India. The study included 95 children diagnosed with MIS-C between November 2020 and December 2022, categorised by the predominant SARS-CoV-2 variant: Alpha, Delta, and Omicron. Key findings showed that gastrointestinal symptoms remained the most common presentation, while respiratory symptoms increased in later waves. The study observed a significant decrease in disease severity markers such as hospital stay duration, fever duration, and pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels over time. However, coronary artery dilatation increased significantly during the Omicron wave, indicating persistent cardiac involvement. The authors concluded that the clinical phenotype of MIS-C evolved across pandemic waves, with reduced systemic disease severity but ongoing changes in cardiac manifestations. These findings underscore the need for continued echocardiographic surveillance and long-term cardiac follow-up for MIS-C patients, even during milder pandemic phases. The study's cross-sectional design and use of established diagnostic criteria provide moderate confidence in its conclusions.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在印度喀拉拉邦中部的一家三级护理教学医院进行了一项横断面观察研究。该研究纳入了 2020 年 11 月至 2022 年 12 月期间入院的 95 名符合 MIS-C 既定诊断标准的儿童。
elements_zh.methods: 根据主要的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变异波将患者分为三组:Alpha(波 1)、Delta(波 2)和 Omicron(波 3)。主要结果指标包括临床特征、实验室参数、超声心动图结果、治疗 模式和疾病严重程度标记。
elements_zh.main_results: 在所有三波中,胃肠道症状仍然是主要表现,而呼吸道症状在后面几波中有所增加。住院时间、发烧时间和 B 型利钠肽原水平在连续几波中显着下降。心包积液也明显减少,而左心功能不全的患病率则呈下降趋势。相比之下,Omicron 波期间冠状动脉扩张显着增加。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: The clinical phenotype of MIS-C evolved across successive COVID-19 waves, with evidence of decreasing systemic disease severity but persistent changes in cardiac involvement.
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Omicron 波期间冠状动脉扩张显着增加,凸显了持续超声心动图 监测 和长期心脏随访的重要性,即使是在大流行的临床较温和阶段。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到横断面设计和潜在混杂因素的限制,但由于对不同大流行浪潮的清晰比较以及既定诊断标准的使用,证据是强有力的。

papers.title: Structural insights into subunit exchange inhibition and ligand-induced dimerization of SARS-CoV-2 main protease.
papers.abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 main protease (M pro ) is an essential homodimeric cysteine protease that mediates viral polyprotein processing and represents a primary therapeutic target for COVID-19 treatment. While peptidomimetic inhibitors such as nirmatrelvir have demonstrated clinical efficacy, their effects on M pro quaternary structure dynamics remain poorly understood. Emerging evidence suggests these compounds may paradoxically promote dimerization, a phenomenon termed ligand-induced dimerization (LID), which could enhance catalytic activity at low inhibitor concentrations. Here, we employed an integrated mass spectrometry platform combining metabolic 15 N labeling with native mass spectrometry (nMS), hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to elucidate the dynamic nature of M pro dimerization and its modulation by peptidomimetic inhibitors. We demonstrate that apo-M pro exists in a dynamic monomer-dimer equilibrium characterized by rapid subunit exchange. Remarkably, peptidomimetic inhibitors, including nirmatrelvir, GC376, and MPI8, kinetically trap the dimeric state, suppressing subunit exchange and stabilizing the dimeric form of M pro . Region-resolved HDX-MS revealed that inhibitor binding induces widespread conformational stabilization extending beyond the active site to the N-finger (residues 1-17) and dimer interface (residues 291-302). A notable transition of exchange mode from bimodal (EX1) to unimodal (EX2) in the N-finger region provided a sensitive structural marker of ligand-induced dimerization. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed that the observed stabilization arises primarily from dimer formation rather than direct ligand contacts. These findings establish a mechanistic basis for inhibitor-stabilized dimerization, identify the N-finger as a dynamic reporter of quaternary structure transitions, and demonstrate the power of integrated mass spectrometry for dissecting complex protein assembly dynamics with therapeutic implications for antiviral drug development.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed an integrated mass spectrometry platform to analyze the dynamic nature of M pro dimerization and its modulation by peptidomimetic inhibitors, focusing on SARS-CoV-2 and its variants.
analysis.methods: The researchers used metabolic 15 N labeling, native mass spectrometry (nMS), hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to examine the structural changes and dimerization dynamics of M pro in response to inhibitors.
analysis.main_results: The results showed that apo-M pro exists in a dynamic monomer-dimer equilibrium with rapid subunit exchange, and that peptidomimetic inhibitors, including nirmatrelvir, GC376, and MPI8, kinetically trap the dimeric state, suppressing subunit exchange and stabilizing the dimeric form of M pro.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings establish a mechanistic basis for inhibitor-stabilized dimerization and highlight the N-finger region as a dynamic reporter of quaternary structure transitions, offering new insights into the structural modulation of M pro by therapeutic agents.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide critical structural insights that can inform the development of more effective antiviral drugs targeting SARS-CoV-2 main protease, with potential implications for improving therapeutic strategies against COVID-19.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro analyses using mass spectrometry and simulations, and the evidence is based on abstract-level reporting, which may not fully capture in vivo dynamics. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the structural dynamics of SARS-CoV-2 main protease (M pro) and its response to peptidomimetic inhibitors. The research highlights the dynamic monomer-dimer equilibrium of apo-M pro and demonstrates that inhibitors like nirmatrelvir can trap the dimeric state, stabilizing it and suppressing subunit exchange. The findings reveal that inhibitor binding induces conformational stabilization beyond the active site, affecting the N-finger and dimer interface. These results offer a mechanistic understanding of how inhibitors modulate M pro dimerization, which has implications for the development of more effective antiviral therapies. However, the study is limited to in vitro analyses and abstract-level reporting, which may not fully reflect in vivo conditions, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在研究严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2主蛋白酶(M pro)的结构动力学及其对拟肽抑制剂的反应,这对于了解其对病毒多蛋白加工的治疗作用至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究采用集成质谱平台来分析 M pro 二聚化的动态性质及其拟肽抑制剂的调节,重点关注 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 及其变体。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用代谢 15 N 标记、天然质谱 (nMS)、氢-氘交换质谱 (HDX-MS) 和分子动力学 (MD) 模拟来检查 M pro 响应抑制剂的结构变化和二聚化动力学。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果表明,apo-M pro 存在于具有快速亚基交换的动态单体-二聚体平衡中,并且拟肽抑制剂(包括 nirmatrelvir、GC376 和 MPI8)在动力学上捕获二聚体状态,抑制亚基交换并稳定 M pro 的二聚体形式。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现为抑制剂稳定的二聚化奠定了机制基础,并强调 N 指区域作为四级结构转变的动态报告者,为治疗药物对 M pro 的结构调节提供了新的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide critical structural insights that can inform the development of more effective antiviral drugs targeting SARS-CoV-2 main protease, with potential implications for improving therapeutic strategies against COVID-19.
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于使用质谱和模拟的体外分析,证据基于抽象水平的报告,可能无法完全捕捉体内动态。证据强度中等。

papers.title: Biosafety level-3 cryo-electron tomography of active severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 virions.
papers.abstract: Understanding the structural properties of pathogenic viruses in their native, infectious state is critical for rational vaccine and drug development. However, conducting cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) under biosafety level 3 (BSL-3) containment presents significant challenges. Here, we established and validated a high-end cryo-EM workflow within a BSL-3 facility, comprehensively integrating facility design, containment measures, sample handling, cryo-transfer systems, and decontamination protocols. To demonstrate the utility and reproducibility of this workflow, we applied cryo-electron tomography to investigate severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 in its native, active state. Our observations confirm that unfixed viral particles display pleomorphic features comparable to those previously reported in fixed or inactivated preparations, validating that these structural characteristics represent native features rather than artifacts of chemical fixation. Furthermore, spatial redistribution of surface spikes was observed. The establishment of this robust BSL-3 cryo-EM workflow provides a practical blueprint for the structural characterization of emerging high-consequence pathogens, supporting pandemic preparedness, vaccine development, and antiviral discovery.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society

Here, we established and validated a high-end cryo-EM workflow within a BSL-3 facility, comprehensively integrating facility design, containment measures, sample handling, cryo-transfer systems, and decontamination protocols. To demonstrate the utility and reproducibility of this workflow, we applied cryo-electron tomography to investigate severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 in its native, active state. Our observations confirm that unfixed viral particles display pleomorphic features comparable to those previously reported in fixed or inactivated preparations, validating that these structural characteristics represent native features rather than artifacts of chemical fixation. Furthermore, spatial redistribution of surface spikes was observed. The establishment of this robust BSL-3 cryo-EM workflow provides a practical blueprint for the structural characterization of emerging high-consequence pathogens, supporting pandemic preparedness, vaccine development, and antiviral discovery.

papers.title: Social support networks of older adults before, during and after the COVID-19 pandemic
papers.abstract: Societies are considerably challenged by population aging, especially when it comes to providing services and support for older adults. Although formal services such as home care and volunteering address some of these needs, the informal social support given by relatives, friends and neighbours is just as vital. In Slovenia, the share of older adults reporting they have no informal social support rose from around 1% in 2002 to 7.8% in 2020, coinciding with the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic. The article examines the prevalence and characteristics of social support network types relied on by older adults in Slovenia between 2002 and 2025, with a special focus on the post-pandemic recovery. To that end, a cross-sectional survey collected ego-centred network data of older adults (65+) in Slovenia in 2002, 2020 and 2025. The samples are representative of both gender and region. The data were analysed using clustering for symbolic data and correspondence analysis. Distinct network types were identified based on the number and characteristics of the support providers, including relationship type, spatial proximity, and frequency of contact across emotional, instrumental and socialising dimensions. The identified types of social support networks are: family dependent, private restricted, local self-contained, locally integrated, and wider community network type, along with the cluster of egos that did not list any alter called “no-listed alters”. Trends regarding the prevalence of these network types suggest that while some were more strongly affected by the COVID-19 pandemic (no-listed alters, local self-contained, wider community), other network types (family dependent, private restricted, locally integrated) appear to reflect longer-term demographic changes. The partial recovery of informal social support is shown by the share of older adults with no social support having dropped to 4.4% by 2025. Nevertheless, persistent inequalities remain, with men in particular revealed to have greater chances of being socially isolated, pointing to the need for social services to provide proactive support targeting these groups.

papers.title: Misinformation-based preventive behaviors during the COVID-19 pandemic in Myanmar: A cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: Widespread misinformation influenced public understanding of disease risk and preventive behaviors during the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly in low-resource and conflict-affected settings such as Myanmar. Although preventive behaviors were generally protective, some actions driven by misinformation may have been ineffective or harmful. Evidence on determinants of misinformation-based preventive behaviors remained limited. This study aimed to examine associations between misinformation-based preventive behaviors (MPB) and sociodemographic characteristics, information sources, social media use, and health belief factors in Myanmar. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among adults residing in Myanmar, with data collected between March and May 2024. Participants were asked to retrospectively report their preventive behaviors during the COVID-19 pandemic period (2020–2022). Data were collected using a structured questionnaire adapted from previous COVID-19 studies. The outcome variable was misinformation-based preventive behaviors, categorized as low (0–2 behaviors) and high (3–4 behaviors) engagement. Independent variables included sociodemographic characteristics, information sources, social media platform use, and selected health belief variables based on the Health Belief Model (HBM). A total of 434 respondents were included in the analysis, of whom 106 (24.4%) reported high engagement in MPB. Use of social media platforms other than Facebook was associated with higher engagement (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 2.30, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.22–4.35). Participants reporting ≤3 hours and 4–6 hours of daily social media use had lower odds of MPB engagement compared with those reporting >6 hours (AOR = 0.46, 95% CI: 0.25–0.86; AOR = 0.48, 95% CI: 0.24–0.95, respectively). Higher self-efficacy was independently associated with greater engagement in MPB (AOR = 1.70, 95% CI: 1.03–2.82). MPB were more strongly associated with information environments and specific health beliefs than with sociodemographic characteristics alone. These findings underscore the importance of addressing misinformation and improving access to reliable health information to reduce engagement in non–evidence-based practices.

papers.title: Methods to Account for Competing Events With Unknown Duration in Health Policy Evaluations: The Case of COVID-19.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare methods for estimating policy effects in the presence of competing events such as COVID-19. STUDY SETTING AND DESIGN: We created a simulation study to evaluate how single interrupted time series (ITS) and comparative interrupted time series (CITS) estimators performed when policy implementation occurred near a competing event (COVID-19). The onset of the competing event was known (March 2020) but the duration was unknown. ITS approaches included assuming different COVID-19 durations (ITS-Assume) or searching for the COVID-19 duration that provided the best fit to the data (ITS-Grid Search). Outcomes included percent bias, power, and Type 1 error. DATA SOURCES AND ANALYTIC SAMPLE: We varied the duration of COVID-19 effects, the time between the policy implementation and COVID-19 onset, and the magnitude and sign of the policy effects relative to COVID-19 (2080 scenarios). Each simulated time series had 99 monthly observations (October 2015-December 2023). PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: CITS had the lowest bias and Type 1 error and had high power across scenarios, except for intercept changes and when assumptions about shared COVID-19 effects between treatment and control groups were violated. ITS-Grid Search had lower bias and Type 1 error than ITS-Assume, which produced biased parameter estimates when the assumptions were incorrect. Estimates were more accurate when the policy was implemented prior to the competing event. CONCLUSIONS: Using estimation approaches that leverage control groups, such as CITS, can mitigate the potential bias of competing events in ITS frameworks, but these approaches are biased when competing event effects differ between treatment and control groups. Searching for the best-fitting competing event duration does not require a control group and outperforms methods that assume the duration of competing event effects a priori. More generally, researchers should be cautious about bias, specification error, and low power when using ITS methods with competing events.

papers.title_zh: Methods to Account for Competing Events With Unknown Duration in Health Policy Evaluations: The Case of COVID-19.
papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVE: To compare methods for estimating policy effects in the presence of competing events such as COVID-19. STUDY SETTING AND DESIGN: We created a simulation study to evaluate how single interrupted time series (ITS) and comparative interrupted time series (CITS) estimators performed when policy implementation occurred near a competing event (COVID-19). The onset of the competing event was known (March 2020) but the duration was unknown. ITS approaches included assuming different COVID-19 durations (ITS-Assume) or searching for the COVID-19 duration that provided the best fit to the data (ITS-Grid Search). Outcomes included percent bias, power, and Type 1 error. DATA SOURCES AND ANALYTIC SAMPLE: We varied the duration of COVID-19 effects, the time between the policy implementation and COVID-19 onset, and the magnitude and sign of the policy effects relative to COVID-19 (2080 scenarios). Each simulated time series had 99 monthly observations (October 2015-December 2023). PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: CITS had the lowest bias and Type 1 error and had high power across scenarios, except for intercept changes and when assumptions about shared COVID-19 effects between treatment and control groups were violated. ITS-Grid Search had lower bias and Type 1 error than ITS-Assume, which produced biased parameter estimates when the assumptions were incorrect. Estimates were more accurate when the policy was implemented prior to the competing event. CONCLUSIONS: Using estimation approaches that leverage control groups, such as CITS, can mitigate the potential bias of competing events in ITS frameworks, but these approaches are biased when competing event effects differ between treatment and control groups. Searching for the best-fitting competing event duration does not require a control group and outperforms methods that assume the duration of competing event effects a priori. More generally, researchers should be cautious about bias, specification error, and low power when using ITS methods with competing events.

papers.title: Epidemiology of influenza before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic in China: An observational study from Zhejiang, China (2010-2023).
papers.abstract: The epidemiology of influenza has shifted in recent years due to COVID-19 social restrictions.However, it remains unclear whether these findings apply to China, where a strict Zero-COVID policy was implemented.We evaluated influenza trends in Zhejiang Province, China from 2010-2023before, during, and after the strict policy.Specifically, using weekly surveillance data (2010-2023), we applied changepoint detection to identify structural shifts and interrupted time-series models to quantify policy impacts by comparing predicted (P) and observed (O) influenza cases based on differences (O -P) and ratios (P/O).Individual-level data (2017-2023; N=24,165 cases) were also analyzed for lineage and demographic shifts.A total of 4,295,302 influenza diagnoses occurred during the study period.During the policy, observed cases dropped by 248,781 cases in 2020 (P/O: 2.40; 95% prediction interval, 2.28 to 2.52), 204,619 in 2021 (1.72; 1.63 to 1.81), and 199,773 in 2022 (1.66; 1.58 to 1.76).Following policy relaxation in 2023, influenza cases exceeded expectations by 148,662 (0.8; 0.76 to 0.84); however, cases in children under 5 still declined by 22,388 (1.08; 1.04 to 1.12).B/Victoria lineage dominated early in the pandemic (>99% of cases in 2021), while influenza A/H3 (55%) and A/H1 (41%) emerged as the most prevalent strains by 2023.China's Zero-COVID policy was associated with changes in influenza transmission dynamics, with explosive outbreaks after relaxation except among young children.Changes in lineage predominance among lineages intensified during and after restrictions, with uncertain long-term implications.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate how the Zero-COVID policy in China affected influenza trends, as the epidemiology of influenza has shifted due to social restrictions from the pandemic, and it remains unclear whether these changes apply to China.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This observational study analyzed weekly surveillance data from Zhejiang Province, China, spanning 2010-2023, including individual-level data from 24,165 cases between 2017-2023. The study focused on influenza diagnoses during the implementation and relaxation of the Zero-COVID policy.
analysis.methods: The researchers applied changepoint detection to identify structural shifts in influenza trends and used interrupted time-series models to quantify the impact of the policy by comparing predicted (P) and observed (O) cases through differences (O - P) and ratios (P/O). Individual-level data were analyzed for lineage and demographic changes.
analysis.main_results: During the Zero-COVID policy, observed influenza cases dropped by 248,781 in 2020 (P/O: 2.40; 95% prediction interval, 2.28 to 2.52), 204,619 in 2021 (1.72; 1.63 to 1.81), and 199,773 in 2022 (1.66; 1.58 to 1.76). After policy relaxation in 2023, cases exceeded expectations by 148,662 (0.8; 0.76 to 0.84), but declines in children under 5 persisted. The B/Victoria lineage dominated early in the pandemic (>99% of cases in 2021), while influenza A/H3 (55%) and A/H1 (41%) became the most prevalent strains by 2023.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study interprets that China's Zero-COVID policy was associated with changes in influenza transmission dynamics, with explosive outbreaks after relaxation except among young children. It highlights the intensification of lineage predominance during and after restrictions, with uncertain long-term implications.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the understanding of how public health policies can influence influenza transmission dynamics and provide insights into the potential for future outbreaks following policy changes, particularly in different age groups.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on surveillance data and the potential for unmeasured confounding factors. The evidence is moderate, as the results are based on observational data and comparisons of predicted versus observed cases.

analysis.summary_en: This observational study from Zhejiang, China, examines how the Zero-COVID policy impacted influenza trends between 2010 and 2023. The researchers used weekly surveillance data and individual-level case data to analyze changes in influenza cases and lineage predominance. They found that during the policy, observed cases dropped significantly in 2020, 2021, and 2022, but increased after relaxation in 2023, with declines in children under 5 persisting. The B/Victoria lineage dominated early in the pandemic, while A/H3 and A/H1 strains became more prevalent by 2023. The study suggests that the Zero-COVID policy altered influenza transmission dynamics, with potential long-term implications. However, the evidence is moderate due to reliance on observational data and possible confounding factors.

elements_en.study_design_and_population: This observational study analyzed weekly surveillance data from Zhejiang Province, China, spanning 2010-2023, including individual-level data from 24,165 cases between 2017-2023. The study focused on influenza diagnoses during the implementation and relaxation of the Zero-COVID policy.
elements_en.methods: The researchers applied changepoint detection to identify structural shifts in influenza trends and used interrupted time-series models to quantify the impact of the policy by comparing predicted (P) and observed (O) cases through differences (O - P) and ratios (P/O). Individual-level data were analyzed for lineage and demographic changes.
elements_en.main_results: During the Zero-COVID policy, observed influenza cases dropped by 248,781 in 2020 (P/O: 2.40; 95% prediction interval, 2.28 to 2.52), 204,619 in 2021 (1.72; 1.63 to 1.81), and 199,773 in 2022 (1.66; 1.58 to 1.76). After policy relaxation in 2023, cases exceeded expectations by 148,662 (0.8; 0.76 to 0.84), but declines in children under 5 persisted. The B/Victoria lineage dominated early in the pandemic (>99% of cases in 2021), while influenza A/H3 (55%) and A/H1 (41%) became the most prevalent strains by 2023.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study interprets that China's Zero-COVID policy was associated with changes in influenza transmission dynamics, with explosive outbreaks after relaxation except among young children. It highlights the intensification of lineage predominance during and after restrictions, with uncertain long-term implications.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the understanding of how public health policies can influence influenza transmission dynamics and provide insights into the potential for future outbreaks following policy changes, particularly in different age groups.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on surveillance data and the potential for unmeasured confounding factors. The evidence is moderate, as the results are based on observational data and comparisons of predicted versus observed cases.
