papers.title: Gender differences regarding body image-related aspects in the general population during the COVID-19 pandemic: a systematic review
papers.abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted daily routines, physical activity, eating behaviors, and social interactions, all of which may have influenced body image. Previous research suggests that body image concerns differ by gender and may be particularly pronounced among sexual and gender minority (SGM) individuals, who face unique challenges due to internalized appearance ideals and societal stigma. This systematic review examined gender differences in body image-related concerns in the general adult population during the pandemic. Supported by: German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (01KX2121). Methods This systematic review was preregistered (PROSPERO CRD42023421727) and conducted according to PRESS, PRISMA guidelines. Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, PsycINFO were searched for original studies published January 2019-July 2024. Studies were eligible if they 1) examined body image-related outcomes during the COVID-19 pandemic and reported gender-specific analyses in non-clinical adult populations. Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross-Sectional Studies. Studies were narratively summarized according to body image-related constructs assessed and the reported gender-specific findings. Results Sixteen studies comprising 9,813 participants were included. Across most studies, women reported greater body dissatisfaction, weight and shape concerns, body shame and guilt, and dysmorphic concerns than men. Men generally reported lower body dissatisfaction and higher body satisfaction and were more likely to perceive their bodies as slimmer or more athletic. However, three studies found no significant gender differences, and one study reported higher body dissatisfaction among men. Longitudinal evidence suggested increases in body dissatisfaction among men over the course of the pandemic, whereas weight concerns decreased among women over time. One study found higher levels of weight- and body-related shame and guilt among gender minority participants compared with cisgender men, while another study reported no association between sexual orientation and body appreciation. Conclusions Women generally reported greater body image-related concerns than men during the COVID-19 pandemic, although findings were not entirely consistent across studies. Evidence regarding SGM individuals remains limited due to their underrepresentation in the literature. Additional longitudinal and gender diverse research is needed to better understand body image changes during public health crises and to inform targeted prevention and intervention.

papers.title_original: Gender differences regarding body image-related aspects in the general population during the COVID-19 pandemic: a systematic review

analysis.scope_and_question: The review addresses how the COVID-19 pandemic (target disease) has affected body‐image related outcomes in the general adult population, focusing on gender differences in dissatisfaction, shame, and related constructs. Its central question is whether women and men differ in body‐image concerns during the pandemic.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The systematic review was preregistered on PROSPERO (CRD42023421727) and followed PRESS and PRISMA guidelines (A5). Searches were conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, and PsycINFO for studies published between January 2019 and July 2024 (A6). Inclusion required original studies reporting gender‐specific analyses of body‐image outcomes in non‐clinical adults during COVID‐19 (A7). Sixteen studies with a total of 9,813 participants met the criteria (A10). Study quality was appraised with the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist (A8).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Across the majority of included studies, women reported higher levels of body dissatisfaction, weight and shape concerns, body shame, guilt, and dysmorphic concerns than men (A11). Men generally showed lower dissatisfaction and higher body satisfaction, often perceiving themselves as slimmer or more athletic (A12). The authors conclude that women generally experienced greater body‐image concerns during the pandemic, despite some inconsistencies (A16).

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review examined gender differences in body‐image concerns among adults during the COVID‐19 pandemic. Sixteen studies (9,813 participants) were identified through comprehensive database searches and assessed for quality. The prevailing evidence shows that women experienced greater body dissatisfaction, weight‐shape concerns, and related shame than men, while men reported higher body satisfaction and a slimmer self‐perception. However, a minority of studies reported no gender effect or even higher dissatisfaction in men, and data on sexual and gender minority groups are limited. Longitudinal insights are scarce, with only one report of rising dissatisfaction in men over time. The authors recommend additional longitudinal, gender‐inclusive investigations to better inform prevention and intervention efforts in future public‐health emergencies.

papers.title_zh: Gender differences regarding body image-related aspects in the general population during the COVID-19 pandemic: a systematic review
papers.source_body_en: Background The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted daily routines, physical activity, eating behaviors, and social interactions, all of which may have influenced body image. Previous research suggests that body image concerns differ by gender and may be particularly pronounced among sexual and gender minority (SGM) individuals, who face unique challenges due to internalized appearance ideals and societal stigma. This systematic review examined gender differences in body image-related concerns in the general adult population during the pandemic. Supported by: German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (01KX2121). Methods This systematic review was preregistered (PROSPERO CRD42023421727) and conducted according to PRESS, PRISMA guidelines. Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, PsycINFO were searched for original studies published January 2019-July 2024. Studies were eligible if they 1) examined body image-related outcomes during the COVID-19 pandemic and reported gender-specific analyses in non-clinical adult populations. Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross-Sectional Studies. Studies were narratively summarized according to body image-related constructs assessed and the reported gender-specific findings. Results Sixteen studies comprising 9,813 participants were included. Across most studies, women reported greater body dissatisfaction, weight and shape concerns, body shame and guilt, and dysmorphic concerns than men. Men generally reported lower body dissatisfaction and higher body satisfaction and were more likely to perceive their bodies as slimmer or more athletic. However, three studies found no significant gender differences, and one study reported higher body dissatisfaction among men. Longitudinal evidence suggested increases in body dissatisfaction among men over the course of the pandemic, whereas weight concerns decreased among women over time. One study found higher levels of weight- and body-related shame and guilt among gender minority participants compared with cisgender men, while another study reported no association between sexual orientation and body appreciation. Conclusions Women generally reported greater body image-related concerns than men during the COVID-19 pandemic, although findings were not entirely consistent across studies. Evidence regarding SGM individuals remains limited due to their underrepresentation in the literature. Additional longitudinal and gender diverse research is needed to better understand body image changes during public health crises and to inform targeted prevention and intervention.

papers.title: Investigation of anti-SARS-CoV-2 multimeric bicyclic peptide inhibitors in a range of preclinical therapeutic settings
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The spread of respiratory viruses, such as influenza and SARS-CoV-2, has presented significant challenges over the last 30 years, with few effective therapeutic options available to this day. Bicyclic peptides represent a unique, modular modality in the antiviral armamentarium against future pandemics. This study utilizes tool molecules to provide a deeper evaluation of multivalent bicyclic (Bicycle) molecule efficacy in several preclinical SARS-CoV-2 challenge settings. We explore both pre-exposure prophylaxis and post-exposure therapeutic settings via subcutaneous and intranasal routes of administration. We contextualize this further in bespoke scenarios where the immune system is compromised, as well as viral transmission. Promisingly, in all studies, we observe efficacy, significantly reducing infectious viral burden at each study endpoint. These data further support the candidacy of Bicycle molecules as a differentiated antiviral therapeutic class in the context of pandemic preparedness. IMPORTANCE The COVID-19 pandemic triggered a rapid wave of innovation, accelerating the delivery of new vaccine technology and antiviral treatments. In our first paper, we described the discovery and molecular optimization of Bicycle molecules as a novel drug class for the potential treatment of SARS-CoV-2. Here, we have performed deeper characterization of these tool molecules in established animal models to evaluate scenarios for deployment, simulating SARS-CoV-2 transmission, testing more convenient delivery routes, such as intranasal, as well as looking at immunocompromised animals. The Bicycle molecules demonstrated positive outcomes in each of these studies and suggest that Bicycle molecules, as convenient and effective antiviral treatments, could be an important addition to help future preparedness against new viral pandemics.

papers.title: From Viral Detection to Disease Measurement: Lessons from COVID-19.
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic demonstrated a fundamental distinction between detecting an infectious stimulus and measuring the disease produced by that stimulus. SARS-CoV-2 establishes infection, whereas COVID-19 reflects the interaction among viral replication, host immunity, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, coagulation and tissue injury. These processes are related but are not interchangeable measurements. A positive molecular test establishes evidence of viral genetic material; it does not, by itself, quantify tissue injury, systemic thromboinflammation or disease severity. Similarly, individual biomarkers measure components of a biological response rather than necessarily defining the complete disease state. Clinical outcomes, including hospitalization and death, provide important measures of consequence but do not necessarily identify the mechanisms that produced them. COVID-19 therefore provides a case study in measurement fidelity: the quantity measured must be distinguished from the biological process that the investigator seeks to understand. Viral evolution, changing population immunity, vaccination, immune imprinting and human behaviour further demonstrate that the relationship between infection and disease changes over time. Future pandemic preparedness should integrate pathogen detection with mechanistically appropriate measurements of host response, tissue injury and clinical outcome, while maintaining explicit boundaries between measurement, inference and causation.
authors: NRP BA BS Matthew R Fleming

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to highlight the distinction between detecting an infectious stimulus and measuring the disease it produces, as demonstrated by the COVID-19 pandemic.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a conceptual analysis of the relationship between viral infection and disease, focusing on SARS-CoV-2 and its associated clinical outcomes.
analysis.methods: The methods involve a review and synthesis of existing knowledge on viral detection, disease measurement, and the factors influencing their relationship, including viral evolution, immunity, and human behavior.
analysis.main_results: The results emphasize that viral genetic material detection does not equate to quantifying tissue injury, systemic thromboinflammation, or disease severity, and that individual biomarkers reflect components of a biological response rather than the complete disease state.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the pandemic has shown the need to distinguish between infection and disease, and that this distinction is crucial for accurate measurement and understanding of the biological processes involved.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the importance of integrating pathogen detection with appropriate measurements of host response, tissue injury, and clinical outcomes to improve pandemic preparedness and public health responses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to conceptual analysis and does not provide empirical data, but it offers a high-level framework for understanding the relationship between infection and disease.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the distinction between detecting an infectious stimulus and measuring the resulting disease, using the COVID-19 pandemic as a case study. It highlights that viral genetic material detection alone does not quantify disease severity or mechanisms. The authors argue that future pandemic preparedness must integrate pathogen detection with mechanistically appropriate measurements of host response and clinical outcomes. The study provides a conceptual framework for understanding the relationship between infection and disease, emphasizing the need to maintain explicit boundaries between measurement, inference, and causation. While the analysis is abstract-based and lacks empirical data, it offers important insights into improving public health strategies. The evidence is moderate in strength due to its conceptual nature and the absence of direct experimental results.

papers.title_zh: From Viral Detection to Disease Measurement: Lessons from COVID-19.
papers.source_body_en: The COVID-19 pandemic demonstrated a fundamental distinction between detecting an infectious stimulus and measuring the disease produced by that stimulus. SARS-CoV-2 establishes infection, whereas COVID-19 reflects the interaction among viral replication, host immunity, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, coagulation and tissue injury. These processes are related but are not interchangeable measurements. A positive molecular test establishes evidence of viral genetic material; it does not, by itself, quantify tissue injury, systemic thromboinflammation or disease severity. Similarly, individual biomarkers measure components of a biological response rather than necessarily defining the complete disease state. Clinical outcomes, including hospitalization and death, provide important measures of consequence but do not necessarily identify the mechanisms that produced them. COVID-19 therefore provides a case study in measurement fidelity: the quantity measured must be distinguished from the biological process that the investigator seeks to understand. Viral evolution, changing population immunity, vaccination, immune imprinting and human behaviour further demonstrate that the relationship between infection and disease changes over time. Future pandemic preparedness should integrate pathogen detection with mechanistically appropriate measurements of host response, tissue injury and clinical outcome, while maintaining explicit boundaries between measurement, inference and causation.

papers.title: Host-Directed p53 and NRF2 Co-Activation Reverses Acute COVID-19 and Long COVID Pathology by Restoring the miR-29 and miR-145 Epigenetic Axis
papers.abstract: Abstract Despite over 524,592 COVID-19 papers indexed in PubMed as documented in our synthesis compilation and widespread vaccine deployment over the past six years, COVID-19 has caused more than 7.11 million officially reported deaths globally—with WHO excess mortality estimates reaching 14.83 million for 2020–2021 alone and cumulative excess death estimates spanning 18.5 to 35.2 million [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]—while leaving an estimated 400 million individuals worldwide with Long COVID (post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2, or PASC) at an approximate $1 trillion annual economic cost [1, 5]. To address the absence of a phase-independent mechanistic therapy, we propose and computationally evaluate a unified host-directed therapeutic framework centered on co-activating the cellular stress-response regulators p53 and NRF2 [1]. Across acute and post-acute phases, SARS-CoV-2 suppresses p53 and NRF2 signaling, depleting miR-29 (which harbors 11 conserved binding sites on the SARS-CoV-2 genome and directly targets IFNG) and miR-145 (which restrains Tissue Factor F3, Semaphorin-3A Sema3a, Granzyme K GZMK, and MYC) while hyperactivating NF-κB [1, 7, 8, 9, 10]. This upstream collapse drives persistent elevations in IFN-γ, Tissue Factor (TF), Sema3a, and Granzyme K (GzmK), promoting myocarditis, thromboembolism, myocardial dysfunction, and age-related tissue remodeling independently of age-associated immune dysfunction [1, 11, 12, 13]. Stiff ordinary differential equation (ODE) simulations (solve_ivp/BDF) parameterized from published turnover kinetics demonstrate that simulated p53/NRF2 co-activation induces a sharp bifurcation switch near an agonist threshold of Uth = 0.4–0.6 under persistent antigenic stimulation, producing a 13.75-fold recovery of miR-29 and a 54.39-fold recovery of miR-145 while suppressing NF-κB by 94.0% and reducing IFN-γ, TF, Sema3a, and GzmK by 98.3% to 99.1% in locked PASC steady states [14]. In an aggressive acute infection simulation (rv = 0.12 h-1), therapy initiated at 24 h lowers 168 h viral load by 46.2% and suppresses the four terminal effectors by 92.0% to 95.1% [14]. Because these quantitative dynamics derive from in silico modeling and cross-study synthesis, key evidentiary caveats remain—including incomplete extraction of individual duplex coordinates for all 11 miR-29 viral sites, cross-species differences in miR-145 validation for GZMK and Sema3a, compartment-specific p53 paradoxes, and the absence of prospective randomized trials testing combined p53/NRF2 agonism in PASC [1, 10, 15].

papers.title_zh: Host-Directed p53 and NRF2 Co-Activation Reverses Acute COVID-19 and Long COVID Pathology by Restoring the miR-29 and miR-145 Epigenetic Axis
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Despite over 524,592 COVID-19 papers indexed in PubMed as documented in our synthesis compilation and widespread vaccine deployment over the past six years, COVID-19 has caused more than 7.11 million officially reported deaths globally—with WHO excess mortality estimates reaching 14.83 million for 2020–2021 alone and cumulative excess death estimates spanning 18.5 to 35.2 million [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]—while leaving an estimated 400 million individuals worldwide with Long COVID (post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2, or PASC) at an approximate $1 trillion annual economic cost [1, 5]. To address the absence of a phase-independent mechanistic therapy, we propose and computationally evaluate a unified host-directed therapeutic framework centered on co-activating the cellular stress-response regulators p53 and NRF2 [1]. Across acute and post-acute phases, SARS-CoV-2 suppresses p53 and NRF2 signaling, depleting miR-29 (which harbors 11 conserved binding sites on the SARS-CoV-2 genome and directly targets IFNG) and miR-145 (which restrains Tissue Factor F3, Semaphorin-3A Sema3a, Granzyme K GZMK, and MYC) while hyperactivating NF-κB [1, 7, 8, 9, 10]. This upstream collapse drives persistent elevations in IFN-γ, Tissue Factor (TF), Sema3a, and Granzyme K (GzmK), promoting myocarditis, thromboembolism, myocardial dysfunction, and age-related tissue remodeling independently of age-associated immune dysfunction [1, 11, 12, 13]. Stiff ordinary differential equation (ODE) simulations (solve_ivp/BDF) parameterized from published turnover kinetics demonstrate that simulated p53/NRF2 co-activation induces a sharp bifurcation switch near an agonist threshold of Uth = 0.4–0.6 under persistent antigenic stimulation, producing a 13.75-fold recovery of miR-29 and a 54.39-fold recovery of miR-145 while suppressing NF-κB by 94.0% and reducing IFN-γ, TF, Sema3a, and GzmK by 98.3% to 99.1% in locked PASC steady states [14]. In an aggressive acute infection simulation (rv = 0.12 h-1), therapy initiated at 24 h lowers 168 h viral load by 46.2% and suppresses the four terminal effectors by 92.0% to 95.1% [14]. Because these quantitative dynamics derive from in silico modeling and cross-study synthesis, key evidentiary caveats remain—including incomplete extraction of individual duplex coordinates for all 11 miR-29 viral sites, cross-species differences in miR-145 validation for GZMK and Sema3a, compartment-specific p53 paradoxes, and the absence of prospective randomized trials testing combined p53/NRF2 agonism in PASC [1, 10, 15].

papers.title: Intranasal azelastine for the treatment and prevention of SARS-CoV-2: A systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis of randomized trials
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Azelastine, a widely used H1-antihistamine with demonstrated antiviral and antiinflammatory activity against severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) in preclinical and early clinical studies, has emerged as a potential repurposed therapy for early infection.This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of intranasal azelastine for the treatment of established SARS-CoV-2 infection and the prevention of incident SARS-CoV-2 infection.AIM To systematically evaluate the randomized evidence on intranasal azelastine for the treatment of established SARS-CoV-2 infection and the prevention of incident SARS-CoV-2 infection, with particular emphasis on virological outcomes, prevention efficacy, and safety.METHODS PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane Library, together with trial registries and preprint servers, were searched through January 16, 2026.Randomized controlled trials evaluating intranasal azelastine vs placebo were identified through January 2026.Treatment efficacy was assessed using changes in SARS-CoV-2 viral load at predefined follow-up time points, while prevention efficacy was assessed using incident polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection.Safety outcomes were synthesized separately.Risk of bias was assessed using RoB-2 and certainty using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation.Randomeffects meta-analysis was used where quantitative pooling was appropriate. RESULTS / 45Three randomized controlled trials involving 754 participants were included.Two treatment trials contributed to the viral-load analyses, while one prevention trial evaluated incident SARS-CoV-2 infection.Among the two treatment trials, moderatecertainty evidence suggested a greater reduction in SARS-CoV-2 viral load at day 3 [mean difference (MD): -0.18, 95% confidence interval (CI): -0.25 to -0.12; I2 = 0%].The difference was smaller at day 5/6 (MD: -0.11, 95%CI: -0.18 to -0.05; I2 = 0%) and was not statistically significant at day 11 (MD: -0.09, 95%CI: -0.26 to 0.07; I2 = 4%).In the prevention trial, PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection occurred in 5/227 participants (2.2%) receiving azelastine vs 15/223 (6.7%) receiving placebo [risk ratio (RR): 0.33, 95%CI: 0.12-0.89].Treatment-only all-adverse event pooling showed RR 0.85 (95%CI: 0.56-1.27;I2 = 61%), whereas the prevention trial showed RR 2.25 (95%CI: 1.64-3.09). CONCLUSIONModerate-certainty evidence suggested an early virological difference with intranasal azelastine in established SARS-CoV-2 infection, particularly at day 3, although the clinical relevance of this surrogate outcome remains uncertain.Evidence for prevention was based on a single randomized trial, while safety findings differed between treatment and prevention populations.Overall, the available evidence is exploratory and insufficient to establish clinical benefit on patient-important outcomes.

RESULTS / 45Three randomized controlled trials involving 754 participants were included.Two treatment trials contributed to the viral-load analyses, while one prevention trial evaluated incident SARS-CoV-2 infection.Among the two treatment trials, moderatecertainty evidence suggested a greater reduction in SARS-CoV-2 viral load at day 3 [mean difference (MD): -0.18, 95% confidence interval (CI): -0.25 to -0.12; I2 = 0%].The difference was smaller at day 5/6 (MD: -0.11, 95%CI: -0.18 to -0.05; I2 = 0%) and was not statistically significant at day 11 (MD: -0.09, 95%CI: -0.26 to 0.07; I2 = 4%).In the prevention trial, PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection occurred in 5/227 participants (2.2%) receiving azelastine vs 15/223 (6.7%) receiving placebo [risk ratio (RR): 0.33, 95%CI: 0.12-0.89].Treatment-only all-adverse event pooling showed RR 0.85 (95%CI: 0.56-1.27;I2 = 61%), whereas the prevention trial showed RR 2.25 (95%CI: 1.64-3.09). CONCLUSIONModerate-certainty evidence suggested an early virological difference with intranasal azelastine in established SARS-CoV-2 infection, particularly at day 3, although the clinical relevance of this surrogate outcome remains uncertain.Evidence for prevention was based on a single randomized trial, while safety findings differed between treatment and prevention populations.Overall, the available evidence is exploratory and insufficient to establish clinical benefit on patient-important outcomes.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examined the efficacy and safety of intranasal azelastine for treating established SARS‐CoV‐2 infection and preventing incident infection, focusing on virological outcomes, prevention efficacy, and safety in randomized trials.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane Library through January 16, 2026 identified randomized controlled trials comparing intranasal azelastine to placebo; risk of bias was assessed with RoB‐2 and certainty with GRADE, and random‐effects meta‐analysis was employed where appropriate.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Moderate‐certainty evidence indicated a greater reduction in SARS‐CoV‐2 viral load at day 3 with intranasal azelastine in established infection, though the clinical relevance of this surrogate outcome remains uncertain.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Evidence for prevention was limited to a single randomized trial, and safety findings varied between treatment and prevention populations, underscoring the exploratory nature of the data.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The current evidence is insufficient to confirm clinical benefit on patient‐important outcomes, highlighting the need for larger, well‐designed trials to clarify efficacy and safety.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and exploratory meta‐analysis evaluated intranasal azelastine for treating and preventing SARS‐CoV‐2 infection. Searches of major databases up to January 2026 yielded three randomized controlled trials (754 participants). Meta‐analysis showed a modest, statistically significant reduction in viral load at day 3 in treatment trials, but the effect waned by day 5/6 and was not significant by day 11. A single prevention trial suggested a 67 % relative risk reduction in PCR‐confirmed infection, yet safety outcomes differed between treatment and prevention groups. Overall, moderate‐certainty evidence points to an early virological benefit, yet the clinical relevance is unclear, and the limited number of trials and heterogeneous safety data preclude definitive conclusions. Further large, rigorously designed studies are required to determine whether intranasal azelastine offers meaningful patient‐important benefits.

papers.title: Comparison of methodological approaches in COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness estimation using observational data
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Target trial emulation (TTE) is a framework to systematically address potential design-related biases in causal inference when using observational data. We estimated vaccine effectiveness (VE) of the Omicron XBB.1.5 booster vaccination against SARS-CoV-2 infection between 2 October 2023 and 2 April 2024 using four TTE approaches. Methods: A hypothetical target trial was designed where eligible participants would be randomly assigned to receive booster vaccination or not. Four approaches were used to emulate this hypothetical trial using data of an ongoing prospective cohort study in the Netherlands. The first and second approach defined time zero as the start of the booster vaccination rollout and considered vaccination as a time-varying variable. The first approach adjusted for confounders by regression adjustment, while the second used inverse probability weighting. The third and fourth approach used multiple time zeros. In the third approach, all persons who received a booster vaccination on a specific day were matched 1:1 to persons who were not (yet) vaccinated on that day. In the fourth approach, confounders were adjusted for using inverse probability weighting. Results: Overall VE was 30% (95%CI:26-34), 28% (24-32), 25% (18-30) and 27% (24-31) in the first, second, third and fourth approach, respectively. VE decreased as time since vaccination increased. Conclusions: Estimated VE was similar across the four approaches. The choice of approach should be based on the model assumptions, estimand of interest, and feasibility.

papers.title: Detection of SARS-CoV-2 in Semen Months After COVID-19: Potential Evidence of Low-Level Replicative Persistence.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Viral persistence is considered one of the key mechanisms driving long COVID symptoms. The male genital tract (MGT), particularly the testis, is an immune-privileged site that may serve as a viral reservoir for SARS-CoV-2. However, the presence of SARS-CoV-2 in semen and its long-term infectiousness remains controversial. OBJECTIVES: We aimed to investigate the long-term presence and potential replicative activity of SARS-CoV-2 in semen, evaluating whether the virus can persist and maintain low-level culture signals in the MGT well beyond the acute phase of infection. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This observational, prospective, cross-sectional study included 38 men treated at Mater Dei Hospital, Brazil, between October 2020 and October 2021, who had recovered from mild to moderate COVID-19 and consented to participate. Semen samples were collected from mildly symptomatic participants at approximately 1 month (15- 45 days), 3 months, and 6 months after symptom onset. The moderately symptomatic group provided a single sample approximately 6 months post-infection. Semen analysis and SARS-CoV-2 detection were performed using RT-qPCR, followed by viral isolation in Vero CCL-81 cells. Potential viral persistence and replication signals were evaluated through immunofluorescence and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). RESULTS: SARS-CoV-2 was detected by RT-qPCR in 21 of 38 patients (55%), with high cycle threshold (Ct 38-39) values observed for more than 6 months post-infection. Following inoculation into Vero cell cultures, a low-level in vitro expansion of viral copies was identified in a subset of samples from mild and moderate patients. The potential presence of the virus was further supported by the presence of viral proteins via immunofluorescence and the identification of structures morphologically compatible with coronavirus-like particles by TEM. CONCLUSION: This study provides evidence of the long-term persistence of viral RNA and culture-derived signals suggestive of restricted or low-level replicative activity in semen. These findings suggest that the MGT may serve as a viral reservoir, highlighting the importance of longitudinal semen analysis for monitoring viral persistence and reservoir dynamics after clinical recovery.

papers.title: Glycoform Distributions and Heparan Sulfate Binding of Intact SARS-CoV-2 Spike Variants by DIA-ECCR Native Mass Spectrometry
papers.abstract: Glycosylation influences the structure, immunogenicity, and evolutionary selection of the SARS CoV 2 spike protein (S), but its extensive heterogeneity has hindered characterization of intact glycoform distributions. Here, we illustrate a data-independent analysis - electron capture charge reduction (DIA-ECCR) native mass spectrometry workflow for direct analysis of intact spike glycoforms across multiple variants. DIA-ECCR resolves variant-dependent differences in glycoform distributions and higher mass subpopulations. Monte Carlo simulations based on published site-specific bottom-up glycoproteomic data reproduce the central mass of the D614G experimental distribution and support a connection between intact and bottom-up measurements, while the broader experimental distributions and a second Gamma subpopulation indicate heterogeneity not captured by the simulations Mass photometry and charge detection mass spectrometry provide orthogonal measurements consistent with the DIA-ECCR results. DIA-ECCR also resolves mass shifts associated with binding of truncated heparan sulfate, demonstrating analysis of a heterogeneous protein:ligand complex. Together, these results outline a practical workflow that combines DIA-ECCR with native mass spectrometry (nMS) for characterizing intact glycoform distributions and ligand binding in highly heterogeneous glycoprotein assemblies, with potential applications in antigen characterization, vaccine design, and biopharmaceutical quality control.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenges in characterizing the extensive heterogeneity of glycoform distributions in the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, which has hindered understanding of its structure, immunogenicity, and evolutionary selection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research introduced a data-independent analysis - electron capture charge reduction (DIA-ECCR) native mass spectrometry workflow to directly analyze intact spike glycoforms across multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants.
analysis.methods: The study utilized DIA-ECCR native mass spectrometry to resolve variant-dependent differences in glycoform distributions and higher mass subpopulations, with Monte Carlo simulations based on site-specific bottom-up glycoproteomic data used to support the findings.
analysis.main_results: Monte Carlo simulations reproduced the central mass of the D614G experimental distribution and supported a connection between intact and bottom-up measurements, while broader experimental distributions and a second Gamma subpopulation indicated heterogeneity not captured by the simulations.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results demonstrate the utility of DIA-ECCR in analyzing heterogeneous protein:ligand complexes, such as those formed with truncated heparan sulfate, and outline a practical workflow for characterizing glycoform distributions and ligand binding.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings have potential applications in antigen characterization, vaccine design, and biopharmaceutical quality control, offering insights into the structural and functional diversity of SARS-CoV-2 spike proteins.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges that Monte Carlo simulations may not fully capture the heterogeneity observed in experimental distributions, suggesting that further validation with additional methods is needed to strengthen the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the challenge of characterizing the extensive heterogeneity of glycoform distributions in the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, which has hindered understanding of its structure and immunogenicity. The research introduces a data-independent analysis - electron capture charge reduction (DIA-ECCR) native mass spectrometry workflow to directly analyze intact spike glycoforms across multiple variants. The methods employed include DIA-ECCR and Monte Carlo simulations based on site-specific bottom-up glycoproteomic data. The main results show that while simulations reproduce the central mass of the D614G experimental distribution, broader experimental distributions and a second Gamma subpopulation indicate heterogeneity not captured by the simulations. The study also demonstrates the analysis of a heterogeneous protein:ligand complex formed with truncated heparan sulfate. These findings outline a practical workflow for characterizing glycoform distributions and ligand binding, with potential applications in vaccine design and biopharmaceutical quality control. The study notes that Monte Carlo simulations may not fully capture the observed heterogeneity, highlighting the need for further validation with additional methods.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决表征 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 刺突蛋白 中糖型分布的广泛异质性的挑战,这阻碍了对其结构、免疫原性和进化选择的理解。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究引入了数据独立分析 - 电子捕获电荷还原 (DIA-ECCR) 原生质谱工作流程,可直接分析多个 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体的完整刺突糖型。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究利用 DIA-ECCR 天然质谱法来解决糖型分布和较高质量亚群中变异依赖性的差异,并使用基于位点特异性自下而上糖蛋白质组数据的蒙特卡罗模拟来支持研究结果。
elements_zh.main_results: 蒙特卡洛模拟再现了 D614G 实验分布的中心质量,并支持完整测量和自下而上测量之间的联系,而更广泛的实验分布和第二个伽马亚群表明模拟未捕获的异质性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结果证明了 DIA-ECCR 在分析异质蛋白:配体复合物(例如用截短的硫酸乙酰肝素形成的复合物)方面的实用性,并概述了表征糖型分布和配体结合的实用工作流程。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现在抗原表征、疫苗 设计和生物制药质量控制方面具有潜在应用,为了解 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 刺突蛋白 的结构和功能多样性提供了见解。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究承认蒙特卡罗模拟可能无法完全捕捉到实验分布中观察到的异质性,这表明需要使用其他方法进一步验证以加强证据。

papers.abstract_zh: 糖基化影响 SARS CoV 2 刺突蛋白 (S) 的结构、免疫原性和进化选择,但其广泛的异质性阻碍了完整糖型分布的表征。在这里,我们展示了一种独立于数据的分析 - 电子捕获电荷还原 (DIA-ECCR) 原生质谱工作流程,用于直接分析多个变体的完整刺突糖型。DIA-ECCR 解决了糖型分布和较高质量亚群中的变异依赖性差异。基于已发布的位点特异性自下而上糖蛋白质组数据的蒙特卡罗模拟再现了 D614G 实验分布的中心质量,并支持完整测量和自下而上测量之间的联系,而更广泛的实验分布和第二个 Gamma 亚群表明模拟未捕获的异质性。质量光度测定和电荷检测质谱提供了与 DIA-ECCR 结果一致的正交测量。DIA-ECCR 还解决了与截短的硫酸乙酰肝素结合相关的质量变化,证明了异质蛋白质:配体复合物的分析。总之,这些结果概述了一个实用的工作流程,将 DIA-ECCR 与天然质谱 (nMS) 相结合,用于表征高度异质性糖蛋白组装体中完整的糖型分布和配体结合,并在抗原表征、疫苗 设计和生物制药质量控制方面具有潜在的应用。

papers.title: Post-COVID-19 Emergence and Spread of Hypertransmissible Cryptosporidium hominis gp60 Subtype IfA12G1R5, Spain.
papers.abstract: COVID-19 pandemic containment measures in 2020 selectively altered established Cryptosporidium hominis anthroponotic transmission in Spain. Rapid emergence and expansion of hypertransmissible human-adapted gp60 subtypes such as IfA12G1R5 and, less markedly, IbA13G3 followed. Conversely, transmission of the largely zoonotic C. parvum remained comparatively stable, yielding a dual epidemiologic scenario in this country.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the impact of the 2020 pandemic containment measures on the transmission dynamics of Cryptosporidium hominis in Spain. It highlights the emergence and spread of hypertransmissible gp60 subtypes, such as IfA12G1R5, as a result of these measures, while noting that the largely zoonotic C. parvum transmission remained stable. The authors interpret this as evidence of pandemic interventions altering anthroponotic transmission patterns. The findings suggest potential implications for surveillance and understanding of Cryptosporidium hominis epidemiology. However, the study is based on abstract-only evidence, which limits the confidence in its conclusions. The research contributes to understanding how public health measures can influence the spread of non-SARS-CoV-2 pathogens, offering insights into the interplay between pandemic responses and other infectious diseases.

papers.title: Rising Tuberculosis Presentations in Ontario, Canada Are Not Explained by Community SARS-CoV-2 Activity: A Population-Based Time-Series Study
papers.abstract: Background: Tuberculosis (TB) notifications have increased in several high-income countries since 2020. Proposed explanations include pandemic related disruption of treatment for latent tuberculosis, changes in population composition, and immune dysfunction following SARS CoV 2 infection. We assessed whether TB presentations increased during the pandemic era and then tested whether community SARS CoV 2 activity was followed by increased mycobacterial disease. Methods: We conducted a population-based ecological time-series study of first TB- and nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM)-coded hospital, emergency-department and ambulatory clinic presentations in the Greater Toronto/Hamilton Area Plus (GTHA+), Ontario (2024 population approximately 11.2 million), from April 2011 through March 2024. NTM served as a comparator because it shares diagnostic pathways with TB but differs epidemiologically. Negative binomial projection and full-series models estimated pandemic-era changes under three alternative trend assumptions. Distributed lag non linear models estimated cumulative rate ratios for standardized community viral activity over 0 to 12 weeks; sensitivity analyses extended the maximum lag to 26 and 52 weeks. Influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) were prespecified comparators; data for five additional viral exposures were obtained after the primary analysis was completed and analysed as exploratory comparisons. Results: We identified 3,985 first TB-coded and 5,214 first NTM-coded acute-care presentations. Across six models, estimated pandemic-era TB increases ranged from 3% to 22%. No model suggested an increased in NTM. SARS-CoV-2 activity was not positively associated with TB (cumulative rate ratio per 1-SD increase over 0 to 12 weeks 0.909, 95% CI 0.822 to 1.006) or NTM (0.953, 0.868 to 1.047). No positive associations were identified in subgroup analyses or with maximum lags of 26 or 52 weeks. Influenza was not associated with either outcome. RSV was associated with TB and NTM; only the RSV/NTM association met the Bonferroni threshold among the prespecified comparisons, and no exploratory associations met the experiment wide threshold. Conclusions: We identified a modest pandemic era increase in TB-coded acute-care presentations in Ontario, Canada, although its estimated size depended on assumptions about underlying trends. NTM-coded presentations did not increase. Community SARS-CoV-2 activity was not positively associated with subsequent TB or NTM presentations at lags of up to one year and did not provide a temporal explanation for the population-level TB increase. Individual-level effects cannot be excluded.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates whether the rise in tuberculosis (TB) notifications in Ontario, Canada, since 2020 can be attributed to community SARS-CoV-2 activity. The researchers conducted a population-based ecological time-series analysis of TB and nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM) presentations from 2011 to 2024. They found a modest increase in TB-coded presentations during the pandemic era, with estimates ranging from 3% to 22%, but no significant association with SARS-CoV-2 activity. NTM-coded presentations did not increase, and no positive associations were found with SARS-CoV-2 or influenza at various lags. The study suggests that community SARS-CoV-2 activity does not explain the TB increase, though individual-level effects cannot be excluded. The findings have implications for understanding TB trends during the pandemic and for public health surveillance.

papers.title: Application of a Human Nasal Mucosa Ex Vivo Culture System to Model Inflammatory Responses
papers.abstract: Introduction The nasal cavity is the entry point of the upper respiratory tract and the primary site of inflammatory responses to inhaled pathogens. Methods Human nasal mucosa (HNM) tissues were obtained from patients undergoing endoscopic nasal surgery. Six HNM specimens from patients with house dust mite (HDM)-allergic rhinitis were used for paired Der p 1 challenge experiments, and 8 chronic rhinosinusitis–derived HNM specimens were used for paired SARS-CoV-2 infection experiments. Histology, Reverse Transcription Quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction, Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay, and bulk RNA sequencing were performed at the indicated time points. Results Cultured HNM maintained structural and functional integrity during short-term ex vivo culture. HDM stimulation enhanced secretory activity and induced IL-4 and IL-5 expression at day 3. Both SARS-CoV-2 variants (HU-1 and Omicron BA.2) produced detectable viral RNA and viral N-protein signals in HNM expressing Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme 2 and Transmembrane Protease Serine 2. Viral inoculation induced an interferon-associated antiviral response, which was most pronounced following HU-1 exposure, although between-variant differences in the measured antiviral markers were not significant. At 3 days postinfection under standardized infection conditions, HU-1 showed higher viral RNA burden and more marked epithelial injury than BA.2 at day 3. Discussion The ex vivo HNM model preserved key structural and cellular features of native nasal mucosa, including an intact epithelial barrier, stromal immune cells, and glandular components, supporting its use as a tissue-level platform that complements conventional 2-dimensional cultures. HDM-sensitized HNM showed Der p 1-associated type 2 responses, whereas the viral arm revealed an antiviral response and exploratory variant-associated differences in epithelial injury. Conclusions Short-term ex vivo HNM may provide a practical tissue-level platform for investigating upper-airway responses to allergen exposure and SARS-CoV-2 infection. It preserves multicellular tissue architecture, while further validation in larger, better-stratified cohorts and extended culture optimization will support broader mechanistic and translational application.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to model inflammatory responses in the nasal cavity to inhaled pathogens, focusing on the role of the nasal mucosa as the primary site of such responses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used six human nasal mucosa specimens from patients with house dust mite (HDM)-allergic rhinitis and eight chronic rhinosinusitis-derived specimens for SARS-CoV-2 infection experiments.
analysis.methods: Histology, Reverse Transcription Quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction, Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay, and bulk RNA sequencing were performed at the indicated time points to assess tissue responses.
analysis.main_results: Cultured HNM maintained structural and functional integrity during short-term ex vivo culture. At 3 days postinfection, HU-1 showed higher viral RNA burden and more marked epithelial injury than BA.2.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The ex vivo HNM model preserved key structural and cellular features of native nasal mucosa, supporting its use as a tissue-level platform for studying upper-airway responses to allergens and SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that this ex vivo model could be valuable for understanding and developing strategies to combat upper-airway inflammation caused by SARS-CoV-2 and allergens.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's results are based on a small sample size and short-term culture, which may limit generalizability. However, the evidence is strong given the direct observation of viral RNA and antiviral responses in HNM.

analysis.summary_en: This study applied an ex vivo human nasal mucosa culture system to model inflammatory responses to inhaled pathogens, specifically allergens and SARS-CoV-2. The research aimed to investigate how nasal tissues respond to allergen exposure and viral infection, with a focus on preserving tissue architecture and function. Six HNM specimens from patients with allergic rhinitis were used for Der p 1 challenge experiments, while eight from chronic rhinosinusitis patients were used for SARS-CoV-2 infection experiments. The methods included histology, RT-qPCR, ELISA, and bulk RNA sequencing. Results showed that cultured HNM maintained structural and functional integrity, and SARS-CoV-2 variants HU-1 and BA.2 induced detectable viral RNA and N-protein signals. HU-1 caused higher viral RNA burden and more epithelial injury than BA.2. The authors interpreted these findings as supporting the use of the HNM model for studying upper-airway responses, highlighting its preservation of key features like the epithelial barrier and immune cells. The study's significance lies in its potential to inform surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for SARS-CoV-2 and allergen-related inflammation. However, the small sample size and short-term culture limit the generalizability of the results, though the evidence is considered strong due to direct observations.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在模拟鼻腔对吸入病原体的炎症反应,重点关注鼻粘膜作为此类反应主要部位的作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用了来自屋尘螨(HDM)过敏性鼻炎患者的六份人类鼻粘膜样本和八份慢性鼻窦炎样本进行严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染实验。
elements_zh.methods: 在指定的时间点进行组织学、逆转录定量聚合酶链反应、酶联免疫吸附测定和批量 RNA 测序,以评估组织反应。
elements_zh.main_results: 培养的 HNM 在短期离体培养过程中保持了结构和功能的完整性。感染后 3 天,HU-1 比 BA.2 显示出更高的病毒 RNA 负荷和更明显的上皮损伤。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 离体 HNM 模型保留了天然鼻粘膜的关键结构和细胞特征,支持其用作组织水平平台来研究上呼吸道对过敏原和 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的反应。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,这种离体模型对于理解和制定对抗 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 和过敏原引起的上呼吸道炎症的策略可能很有价值。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的结果基于小样本量和短期培养,这可能会限制普遍性。然而,考虑到 HNM 中病毒 RNA 和 抗病毒药物 反应的直接观察,证据是强有力的。

papers.title: Understanding the Support Needs of People With Long COVID: A Qualitative Study in Aotearoa New Zealand.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Long COVID is a multi-system condition that affects an increasing number of individuals. Little is known about the support needs of people living with long COVID in Aotearoa New Zealand. This study aimed to explore the lived experiences and healthcare access challenges of people with long COVID to better inform service design. METHODS: Co-design methodology was used, informed by the Stanford Design Thinking process and knowledge mobilisation approaches. Participants were recruited via snowballing, through professional networks and support groups. People with lived experience of long COVID were invited to participate in a 2-h workshop, facilitated by researchers, conducted between March and September 2024. Participants were asked to create a depiction of their experience of long COVID and describe their creation to the group; descriptions were audio-recorded, transcribed and thematically analysed. The inclusion of people with lived experience of long COVID as co-investigators ensured that the study was designed and conducted to forefront their knowledge and experience. RESULTS: Eight workshops were conducted, including 30 participants, between March and August 2024. Of these, 25 (83%) were female; of the 25 who provided their age, most were aged 45 to 64 years (n = 18, 72%), four (16%) were aged 25 to 44 years and three (12%) aged 65 years or older. Five key themes emerged: (i) lack of assistance; (ii) systemic barriers; (iii) absence of long COVID clinics; (iv) financial strain; and (v) low quality of care. A sixth theme identified personal coping strategies. CONCLUSIONS: Individuals with long COVID in Aotearoa New Zealand face major barriers to care, including inadequate services, financial hardship, and fragmented healthcare pathways. Findings support improved pathways and primary health care education in long COVID. A person-centred, coordinated, and accessible model of care is needed. LIVED EXPERIENCE OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: The study was designed with two people with lived experience of long COVID included as co-investigators, and a further one on the Advisory Board. All participants had lived experience of long COVID.

analysis.methods: People with lived experience of long COVID were invited to participate in a 2-h workshop, facilitated by researchers, conducted between March and September 2024. The inclusion of people with lived experience of long COVID as co-investigators ensured that the study was designed and conducted to forefront their knowledge and experience. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more accessible and coordinated healthcare models for individuals with long COVID, highlighting the need for improved support systems and education within primary health care.

analysis.summary_en: This qualitative study explores the lived experiences and healthcare access challenges of individuals with long COVID in Aotearoa New Zealand. Using a co-design methodology, 30 participants were recruited through snowballing and participated in workshops to share their experiences. Five key themes emerged, highlighting systemic barriers, lack of assistance, absence of long COVID clinics, financial strain, and low quality of care. The study suggests the need for improved healthcare pathways and education for long COVID patients. While the findings provide valuable insights, the moderate evidence strength is due to the small sample size and reliance on self-reported data.

papers.title_zh: 了解 长新冠 患者的支持需求:新西兰奥特罗亚的定性研究。
papers.source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: Long COVID is a multi-system condition that affects an increasing number of individuals. Little is known about the support needs of people living with long COVID in Aotearoa New Zealand. This study aimed to explore the lived experiences and healthcare access challenges of people with long COVID to better inform service design. METHODS: Co-design methodology was used, informed by the Stanford Design Thinking process and knowledge mobilisation approaches. Participants were recruited via snowballing, through professional networks and support groups. People with lived experience of long COVID were invited to participate in a 2-h workshop, facilitated by researchers, conducted between March and September 2024. Participants were asked to create a depiction of their experience of long COVID and describe their creation to the group; descriptions were audio-recorded, transcribed and thematically analysed. The inclusion of people with lived experience of long COVID as co-investigators ensured that the study was designed and conducted to forefront their knowledge and experience. RESULTS: Eight workshops were conducted, including 30 participants, between March and August 2024. Of these, 25 (83%) were female; of the 25 who provided their age, most were aged 45 to 64 years (n = 18, 72%), four (16%) were aged 25 to 44 years and three (12%) aged 65 years or older. Five key themes emerged: (i) lack of assistance; (ii) systemic barriers; (iii) absence of long COVID clinics; (iv) financial strain; and (v) low quality of care. A sixth theme identified personal coping strategies. CONCLUSIONS: Individuals with long COVID in Aotearoa New Zealand face major barriers to care, including inadequate services, financial hardship, and fragmented healthcare pathways. Findings support improved pathways and primary health care education in long COVID. A person-centred, coordinated, and accessible model of care is needed. LIVED EXPERIENCE OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: The study was designed with two people with lived experience of long COVID included as co-investigators, and a further one on the Advisory Board. All participants had lived experience of long COVID.

papers.title: Persistent Fungal Mortality in the United States Following the COVID-19 Pandemic Peak, 2022-2025.
papers.abstract: Objectives: Fungal infection–associated deaths increased in the United States during the COVID-19 pandemic, but mortality patterns after the pandemic peak are not well-characterized. We analyzed national mortality data to assess whether fungal mortality remained elevated during 2022-2025 and to describe demographic, geographic, pathogen-specific, and underlying cause-of-death patterns after the COVID-19 pandemic peak. Methods: We analyzed National Vital Statistics System multiple-cause-of-death data for 2022-2025. We defined fungal deaths as deaths with a fungal pathogen listed as an underlying or contributing cause of death and summarized deaths by year, month, pathogen, COVID-19 association, underlying cause of death, demographic characteristics, and US Census division. We used 2018-2019 (prepandemic) and 2021 (peak) as reference periods for selected comparisons. Results: During 2022-2025, a total of 30 225 fungal deaths occurred (annual average = 7556). The annual age-adjusted mortality rate per 100 000 population increased from 1.2 in 2018-2019 to 1.5 in 2020 and 1.9 in 2021, and remained between 1.8 and 1.9 during 2022-2025. COVID-19–associated fungal deaths declined after early 2022, but overall fungal mortality remained stable. During 2022-2025, the most common underlying causes of death among fungal deaths were malignant neoplasms, HIV disease, and diseases of the heart; the most commonly specified pathogens were Candida and Aspergillus . Mortality rates varied by age, sex, race and ethnicity, and region. Conclusions: Fungal mortality remained elevated after the COVID-19 pandemic peak despite declines in COVID-19–associated fungal deaths. Continued efforts to monitor fungal disease–related mortality are important to inform efforts to enhance diagnostic capacity and surveillance to better characterize and ultimately reduce the impact of fungal diseases.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines fungal mortality trends in the United States during 2022-2025, following the peak of the COVID-19 pandemic. It finds that fungal mortality rates remained elevated despite a decline in deaths directly linked to COVID-19. The research highlights the importance of continued monitoring of fungal disease-related mortality to improve diagnostic capacity and surveillance. The study uses national mortality data and defines fungal deaths based on the presence of fungal pathogens as underlying or contributing causes. The results show that overall fungal mortality remained stable, with variations observed by age, sex, race and ethnicity, and region. The most common underlying causes of death were malignant neoplasms, HIV disease, and heart diseases, while the most frequently specified pathogens were Candida and Aspergillus. The authors conclude that fungal mortality remained high post-pandemic, emphasizing the need for ongoing efforts to address fungal diseases.

papers.title_zh: Persistent Fungal Mortality in the United States Following the COVID-19 Pandemic Peak, 2022-2025.
papers.source_body_en: Objectives: Fungal infection–associated deaths increased in the United States during the COVID-19 pandemic, but mortality patterns after the pandemic peak are not well-characterized. We analyzed national mortality data to assess whether fungal mortality remained elevated during 2022-2025 and to describe demographic, geographic, pathogen-specific, and underlying cause-of-death patterns after the COVID-19 pandemic peak. Methods: We analyzed National Vital Statistics System multiple-cause-of-death data for 2022-2025. We defined fungal deaths as deaths with a fungal pathogen listed as an underlying or contributing cause of death and summarized deaths by year, month, pathogen, COVID-19 association, underlying cause of death, demographic characteristics, and US Census division. We used 2018-2019 (prepandemic) and 2021 (peak) as reference periods for selected comparisons. Results: During 2022-2025, a total of 30 225 fungal deaths occurred (annual average = 7556). The annual age-adjusted mortality rate per 100 000 population increased from 1.2 in 2018-2019 to 1.5 in 2020 and 1.9 in 2021, and remained between 1.8 and 1.9 during 2022-2025. COVID-19–associated fungal deaths declined after early 2022, but overall fungal mortality remained stable. During 2022-2025, the most common underlying causes of death among fungal deaths were malignant neoplasms, HIV disease, and diseases of the heart; the most commonly specified pathogens were Candida and Aspergillus . Mortality rates varied by age, sex, race and ethnicity, and region. Conclusions: Fungal mortality remained elevated after the COVID-19 pandemic peak despite declines in COVID-19–associated fungal deaths. Continued efforts to monitor fungal disease–related mortality are important to inform efforts to enhance diagnostic capacity and surveillance to better characterize and ultimately reduce the impact of fungal diseases.

papers.title: Genomic surveillance reveals age-structured SARS-CoV-2 transmission across settings.
papers.abstract: Understanding respiratory virus transmission requires integrating pathogen genomic data with detailed epidemiological context. We analyzed >85,000 SARS-CoV-2 genomes linked to epidemiological data collected in Massachusetts from November 2021 to January 2023. Collected in 666 settings, including schools, colleges, and skilled nursing facilities, this dataset enabled direct comparison of within-setting transmission to community-wide risk. Elevated transmission was concentrated in specific age-defined subpopulations-older adolescents in schools, undergraduates in colleges, and residents in nursing facilities-with little additional risk among other groups, notably including staff. Young adults, particularly in colleges, played a disproportionate role in spread, and new viral lineages consistently expanded first within this group. Viral spread followed reproducible urban-to-rural gradients, and vaccination was associated with reduced onward transmission. We further estimated sequencing thresholds required for timely detection of emerging variants. Together, these findings reveal consistent demographic and spatial structure in SARS-CoV-2 transmission that can inform viral respiratory pathogen genomic surveillance.

papers.abstract: In the version of this article initially published, in Fig. 2d, the red triangle depicting vaccine administration at day 17 originally appeared at day 20; in Fig. 5o, the colours of the red and blue traces in the plot were interchanged; in Extended Data Fig. 3h,i, the red and blue colour keys (currently, blue for vaccine, red for no vaccine) were interchanged. 3b legend, in the text now reading “vaccine days 3, 6, 21,” 21 replaces the original “17,” and in the Fig. 3k legend, now reading “vaccine days 3, 6, 20,” 20 replaces the original “21.” In the first sentence of the Methods “Cox proportional hazards regression” section, in the text now reading “For Cox proportional hazards regression, exposures defined relative to an index date...,” “exposures defined relative to an index date” replaces the original “time-dependent variables were defined.” In the first paragraph of the Methods and in the Reporting Summary, data collection timelines have been updated to say “The data-collection cut-off was 1 September 2024 for the NSCLC and melanoma datasets and 1 January 2025 for the tissue agnostic dataset.” Finally, the Acknowledgements have been amended to include the statement that G.A. were supported by the CPRIT Research Training Award CPRIT Training Program (RP210028). The changes have been made in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

papers.title: Neurological manifestations in pediatric COVID-19: a comparative single-center study.
papers.abstract: Objective To compare clinical characteristics, investigations, management, and outcomes of hospitalized children with SARS-CoV-2 infection with and without neurological involvement, and to determine whether neurological disease reflects systemic severity or a distinct clinical pattern. Methods We conducted a retrospective observational study of children aged 1 month-16 years with laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection admitted to a tertiary pediatric center between June 2022 and June 2023. Patients were divided into those with neurological manifestations (ND group, n = 24) and those without neurological involvement (non-ND group, n = 23). Demographic features, clinical presentation, laboratory and neuroimaging findings, treatment, and outcomes were compared. Results Children with neurological involvement were significantly older (median 5.75 vs. 3.00 years, p = 0.022) and less likely to present with fever or systemic inflammatory features. They demonstrated lower inflammatory markers and significantly less cardiac involvement, including dilated cardiomyopathy. papers.title: Disparities During the COVID-19 Pandemic in SARS-CoV-2 Testing Increased After a Federal Government's At-Home Testing Distribution Program Compared with Before in a U.S. Urban Setting.
papers.abstract: Diagnostic testing is essential for controlling the transmission of infectious diseases. During the COVID-19 pandemic, testing became widely available in the United States. However, the association between a federal at-home COVID-19 rapid antigen test distribution program and sociodemographics and COVID-19 testing remains unknown. This secondary analysis aims to (1) assess the association between the federal at-home testing program and testing uptake and (2) examine associations, including interactions with the testing program, between sociodemographic characteristics, testing experience, and COVID-19 testing. We analyzed baseline data collected from February 2021 to November 2022 in a randomized comparative effectiveness parent trial conducted in a mid-Atlantic U.S. Logistic regression models with robust standard errors were used. Overall, 79.9% (1486) of participants reported receiving a COVID-19 test. Exposure to the federal testing program (odds ratio [OR] = 2.25; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.61, 3.13), higher education (OR = 1.36; 95% CI: 1.02, 1.80), private health insurance (OR = 2.03; 95% CI: 1.41, 2.92), higher household income (OR = 1.49; 95% CI: 1.06, 2.09), and ease of testing access (OR = 1.40; 95% CI: 1.04, 1.87) were significantly associated with testing. After adjustment, private insurance (adjusted OR [aOR] = 1.61; 95% CI: 1.12, 2.31) and higher income (aOR = 1.50; 95% CI: 1.12, 2.02) remained associated with testing. The adjusted odds of COVID-19 testing were 2-fold higher (aOR = 2.21; 95% CI: 1.21, 4.04) for high-income (vs. low-income) households during the federal at-home COVID-19 rapid antigen testing program than before its implementation. Disparities in COVID-19 testing by socioeconomic status increased during the federal testing program compared with the period before its implementation. Ensuring equitable access to diagnostic testing remains critical for an effective public health response.

This secondary analysis aims to (1) assess the association between the federal at-home testing program and testing uptake and (2) examine associations, including interactions with the testing program, between sociodemographic characteristics, testing experience, and COVID-19 testing. We analyzed baseline data collected from February 2021 to November 2022 in a randomized comparative effectiveness parent trial conducted in a mid-Atlantic U.S. Logistic regression models with robust standard errors were used. Overall, 79.9% (1486) of participants reported receiving a COVID-19 test. Exposure to the federal testing program (odds ratio [OR] = 2.25; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.61, 3.13), higher education (OR = 1.36; 95% CI: 1.02, 1.80), private health insurance (OR = 2.03; 95% CI: 1.41, 2.92), higher household income (OR = 1.49; 95% CI: 1.06, 2.09), and ease of testing access (OR = 1.40; 95% CI: 1.04, 1.87) were significantly associated with testing. After adjustment, private insurance (adjusted OR [aOR] = 1.61; 95% CI: 1.12, 2.31) and higher income (aOR = 1.50; 95% CI: 1.12, 2.02) remained associated with testing. The adjusted odds of COVID-19 testing were 2-fold higher (aOR = 2.21; 95% CI: 1.21, 4.04) for high-income (vs. low-income) households during the federal at-home COVID-19 rapid antigen testing program than before its implementation. Disparities in COVID-19 testing by socioeconomic status increased during the federal testing program compared with the period before its implementation. Ensuring equitable access to diagnostic testing remains critical for an effective public health response.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines how a federal at-home SARS-CoV-2 rapid antigen test distribution program affected disparities in testing during the COVID-19 pandemic in a U.S. urban setting. It found that overall testing uptake was high, with significant associations between testing and factors such as private insurance, higher income, and education. However, disparities by socioeconomic status increased during the program compared to before. The authors emphasize the importance of equitable access to testing for effective public health responses. The study is a secondary analysis of baseline data from a randomized trial, using logistic regression models with robust standard errors. While the findings are informative, they are based on observational data and adjusted models, which limits the strength of the evidence. The results suggest that targeted interventions are needed to address testing disparities and ensure broader access to diagnostic services.

papers.title: First-hand Alcohol-Related Harms in Hong Kong University Dormitories: A Serial Cross-sectional Study Comparing the Normative, Social Unrest, and COVID-19 Pandemic Periods.
papers.abstract: Between September 2018 and June 2021, we conducted serial cross-sectional surveys of university dormitory residents in Hong Kong (n = 2659). Drinking behaviors and first-hand harms were examined across a normative period, time of protests, and the COVID-19 pandemic. Drinking levels remained steady between the normative and protest periods but increased during the pandemic, and the proportions reporting drinking-related harms were 57.1%, 53.9%, and 62.5%, respectively. Binge drinking was associated with high first-hand harms across 3 periods (adjusted odds ratio [AOR]: 3.46-5.76). Having a drinking roommate was also correlated with harms during the normative period (AOR = 1.66). During the protests, underage drinking history and university location were associated with high first-hand harms (AOR: 1.69 and 1.82). During the COVID-19 pandemic, weekend dormitory residence and low alcohol-related knowledge were significant factors (AOR: 2.78 and 2.85). The findings indicate the need for context-specific alcohol harm reduction strategies in East Asian university dormitories.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study examines first-hand alcohol-related harms among university dormitory residents in Hong Kong during three distinct periods: the normative period, the time of social unrest (protests), and the COVID-19 pandemic. The central question is whether alcohol-related behaviors and their associated harms differ across these periods.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The study is a serial cross-sectional survey conducted between September 2018 and June 2021, involving 2659 participants. It compares drinking behaviors and first-hand harms across three time periods: normative, social unrest, and the pandemic. The methodology includes statistical analysis of associations using adjusted odds ratios.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study found that drinking levels remained stable between the normative and protest periods but increased during the pandemic. The proportions of participants reporting alcohol-related harms were 57.1%, 53.9%, and 62.5% for the normative, protest, and pandemic periods, respectively. Binge drinking was consistently associated with higher first-hand harms across all three periods.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study does not provide detailed information on the mechanisms linking alcohol consumption to first-hand harms or on the effectiveness of interventions. It also does not explore the role of cultural or policy factors in shaping drinking behaviors during these periods.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings suggest the need for context-specific alcohol harm reduction strategies in East Asian university dormitories, particularly during periods of social and health crises like the pandemic.

analysis.summary_en: This serial cross-sectional study conducted between September 2018 and June 2021 analyzed alcohol-related harms among university dormitory residents in Hong Kong during three distinct periods: the normative period, the time of social unrest (protests), and the COVID-19 pandemic. The study found that drinking levels remained stable between the normative and protest periods but increased during the pandemic. The proportions of participants reporting alcohol-related harms were 57.1%, 53.9%, and 62.5% for the normative, protest, and pandemic periods, respectively. Binge drinking was consistently associated with higher first-hand harms across all three periods. The study highlights the need for context-specific alcohol harm reduction strategies in East Asian university dormitories, especially during health and social crises. However, it does not explore the underlying mechanisms or the effectiveness of interventions.
